item.title: 'He still has magic in his boots' - Maddison shows Spurs what they were missing
item.description: James Maddison says he has "so much more to give" Tottenham after he marked his first start in nearly 18 months with a stunning goal that helped Spurs to their first Premier League win of the season.

item.title: Purdy makes NFL history as 49ers beat Commanders to stay perfect
item.description: Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass, Christian McCaffrey ran for two scores and the San Francisco 49ers held on to beat the Washington Commanders 23-17 for their sixth straight win to start the season on Monday night.
item.content:encoded: Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass, Christian McCaffrey ran for two scores and the San Francisco 49ers held on to beat the Washington Commanders 23-17 for their sixth straight win to start the season on Monday night.

item.title: Commanders’ MNF loss to 49ers brings historic embarrassment to NFC East
item.description: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Commanders’ MNF loss to 49ers brings historic embarrassment to NFC East appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Commanders ’ 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football did more than deepen their early-season struggles. It completed one of the most embarrassing stretches in NFC East history. According to league data highlighted by Ari Meirov of MySportsUpdate, the division became the first since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger to go winless in consecutive weeks when every team played. Across Weeks 5 and 6, the Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys, New York Giants, and Commanders combined for an astonishing 0-7-1 record. Washington’s defeat sealed that unwanted milestone. The NFC East is the first division since the 1970 merger to go winless in back-to-back weeks with every team playing. pic.twitter.com/G2ZBiRoblG — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 20, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Commanders mounted a second-half rally behind Jayden Daniels . He helped produce two touchdowns. However, they could not complete the comeback in Santa Clara. They were just unable to establish a consistent ground game. Washington also had mounting injuries , including a devastating knee injury to top receiver Terry McLaurin. The result dropped Washington to 1-4-1 and left the entire division searching for answers. This division’s collective collapse has become an uncomfortable midseason storyline. Washington’s broader 2026 campaign has been equally frustrating. After opening with consecutive divisional losses to Philadelphia and Dallas, the Commanders earned their lone victory in a Week 3 shootout against Seattle. They subsequently lost to Indianapolis. The Commanders then settled for an overtime tie against the Giants, and they fell to the unbeaten 49ers. Daniels has continued to display poise and playmaking ability. That said, inconsistent protection, injuries, and defensive breakdowns have undermined the team’s progress. The upcoming Week 7 bye offers Washington a chance to regroup and address glaring weaknesses. Yet the NFC East’s historic two-week skid makes clear that the Commanders are not alone in their struggles. For now, the entire division has plenty of work to do before it can reclaim its competitive reputation. Related: Of course the Pat McAfee Commanders-49ers MNF broadcast was unhinged Related: Commanders’ Dan Quinn ‘definitly knew’ it was 4th down during viral MNF snafu

item.title: ‘Terrible PR Apology,’ ‘You Should Be Fired’ — Super Bowl Champion Faces Fierce Backlash After Addressing ‘Disgusting’ Comments on Jalen Hurts
item.description: Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) before kick off against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field. © Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Monday brought a reality check for Michael Robinson. By evening, the NFL Network analyst apologized to Jalen Hurts, the Philadelphia Eagles, and their fans for what he said about the QB’s blood clot. Earlier, the team and Hurts’ agent had revealed that his diagnosis had changed to deep vein thrombosis, with clots in both lungs, which was concerning. Fans, then, weren’t ready to accept the apology, as some called for Robinson to be fired. NFL Fans React as Michael Robinson Apologizes for Controversial Remarks Against Jalen Hurts On “NFL GameDay Kickoff” on Thursday, Oct. 15, the day the Eagles ruled Hurts out of their Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers, Robinson, a former Seattle Seahawks fullback who won a Super Bowl in 2014, gave his own read on why Hurts was out. “If I’m Jalen Hurts, or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp, I’m saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too,’ … And I’m not saying a superficial blood clot isn’t serious. I’m not saying that, but I would advise all of our viewers to Google ‘superficial blood clot’ as opposed to a real blood clot.” Robinson’s apology came after Monday’s update on Hurts’ condition. “My comments were wrong. No excuse,” he wrote, adding in a longer statement, “They were unfounded and I never should’ve speculated on a health issue of a player nor his commitment to his team.” Victor Williams, a writer for The Eagles Wire, minced no words in his reply: “Apology not accepted. Never speak again.” One fan was just as blunt about the apology itself: “Terrible PR apology; enjoy being unemployed in a few months.” Tyler Lauletta of Awful Announcing saw it differently, writing “Good on Robinson for offering a real apology” in his piece on the episode. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Another fan went further: “You should be fired. Can’t even apologize on live TV where you insulted him?” Another fan made the same demand: “Fire this man.” This fan took issue with the timing: “Only took him almost dying for you to apologize.” One more fan had a parting message for Robinson: “Hurts will get better. Your reputation is permanently tarnished.” Hurts first reported a problem with his calf on Oct. 8, four days after he was cleated in a Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. In London on Oct. 10, doctors found what the Eagles called a superficial blood clot in his left calf. He was cleared to play the next day and went 21-of-40 for 220 yards and a 62-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper in a 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars with a PFN QB Impact Score of 70.2, #21 in the league. Can’t even apologize on live TV where you insulted him?” Another fan made the same demand: “Fire this man.” This fan took issue with the timing: “Only took him almost dying for you to apologize.” One more fan had a parting message for Robinson: “Hurts will get better. Your reputation is permanently tarnished.” Hurts first reported a problem with his calf on Oct. 8, four days after he was cleated in a Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. In London on Oct. 10, doctors found what the Eagles called a superficial blood clot in his left calf. A follow-up exam on Wednesday, Oct. 14, showed the clot had moved. DIVE IN: PFN’s Free NFL HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More The team placed Hurts on injured reserve on Saturday, Oct. 17, and Monday’s update showed his condition was more serious. He is clinically stable and is taking blood thinners, which keep him out of contact activities, including football, until he is off them. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season and that his recovery is expected to take three months. Before the clot sidelined him, Hurts had completed 89 of 154 passes for 933 yards on the season, with eight touchdowns and three interceptions. He added 107 yards and a score on 23 carries. Through Week 6, his 57.8% completion rate ranks 31st of 33 qualified quarterbacks, and Pro Football Network’s NFL QB Impact Grade has him at 69.6, 22nd of 34 graded quarterbacks. Next up for the Eagles is a Week 7 home game against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night, Oct. 26, at Lincoln Financial Field, followed by a trip to face the Washington Commanders on Nov. 1. item.title: Angel Reese Answers With 30 Points and 16 Rebounds as the Atlanta Dream Win Their First Finals Game Ever
item.description: Angel Reese racked up 30 points and 16 rebounds as the Atlanta Dream recorded their first Finals win, beating the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 on Monday night at Chase Center to tie the series. The Dream had lost 10 straight Finals matches, succumbing in Game 1 on Saturday, 68-64. Seattle and Minnesota swept them in 2010 and 2011 and 2013, respectively. Alongside the 30 points, Reese added three assists, two blocks, and a steal, going 10-for-16 from the field. The Dream forward is now the youngest in WNBA history, finishing with 20 points and 10 rebounds at 24 years and 166 days. She is also the third to record 30 points and 15 rebounds in one Finals game. Reese scored all 14 of her points in the first half in Game 1 and took only three shots in the 26 minutes remaining as Atlanta began trailing. “I let my team down last game, not really contributing as much as I could in the second half,” Reese said. “I wanted to make sure that I came out tonight and left my mark and do what I could to win, and I think I did that tonight.” Dream coach Karl Smesko said that he fixed his eye on Reese while entering the locker room before the match and encouraged him with, “I like this look.” “She was fantastic on both ends of the floor, a superior performance,” Smesko said. In her maiden season with the Dream after the trade in April with the Chicago Sky for the first-round draft picks in 2027 and 2028, Reese delivered a memorable performance that turned the series around. Earlier this month, she became the Dream’s first-ever Defensive Player of the Year and followed it with a league record-breaking performance: 521 rebounds and 206 offensive rebounds. The Dream’s defense matched the mood, holding Golden State to 34.4 percent shooting as the former registered 19 fast-break points. Rhyne Howard recorded a Finals-record six steals, making up for the Valkyries’ errors with 24 points. The Dream made sure of the lanes against Golden State all game, forcing the Valkyries to make different choices than in Game 1, when they won the turnover battle 12-8. Atlanta led 39-37 at halftime despite being in foul trouble with two of its stars. Howard had four fouls in the first half, and Reese was playing with three after earning the third midway through the second quarter. At halftime, Reese had 15 points and Howard three. “We feed off her energy,” Jordin Canada said of Reese. “She was talking to us the whole game, keeping us confident.” Canada recorded 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds, though he believes he could have done better. Allisha Gray added 18 points. Even in scoring only four out of 16 from the floor in the third quarter, Atlanta managed to create some separation. This was mostly due to fouls and going 12-12 from the free-throw line in the quarter. Their defense also matched the focus by keeping Golden State scoreless, missing 11 of 15 without committing any fouls that sent a Valkyries player to the foul line. Howard had four fouls in the first half, and Reese was playing with three after earning the third midway through the second quarter. Allisha Gray added 18 points. Even in scoring only four out of 16 from the floor in the third quarter, Atlanta managed to create some separation. This was mostly due to fouls and going 12-12 from the free-throw line in the quarter. Their defense also matched the focus by keeping Golden State scoreless, missing 11 of 15 without committing any fouls that sent a Valkyries player to the foul line. Howard and Reese earned no fouls after the previous quarter. Reese did not shoot for nearly four minutes early in the quarter after Kiah Stokes blocked her first shot attempt in the second half. Tied with the game, she drove to the hoop for a score and made the free throw, starting an 18-4 run to end the quarter with Atlanta leading 60-46. Reese scored nine points in the run and recorded 24 points and 11 rebounds in the first three quarters. “Her rebound, her fight, were at a high level tonight,” Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said about Reese. The Dream did not ease off in the fourth quarter, with fears haunting them from the first game as they went into the last quarter down by five. They scored just 8 points, going 2-for-19 from the floor. Canada and DeWanna Bonner each sank two free throws in the first minute of the fourth quarter to take a 64-46 lead, and Atlanta never trailed by more than 14 in the remainder of the match. Tiffany Hayes topped the Golden State side with 14 points and Stokes with 11 rebounds and four blocks. Valkyries reserves outscored Atlanta 33-11 but lost their first home match this season. The Valkyries are ranked as the No. In their second season as an expansion side, the No. 2 seed Valkyries stormed to the Finals by sweeping the defending champions Las Vegas Aces. The No. 4 Dream swept Washington and New York to reach this stage. Game 3 is on Wednesday at State Farm Arena, the sold-out arena, with high hopes. It will give Atlanta a chance to take its first lead in the series and be just two wins off the championship. “It’s just a start,” Reese said. “We have the city behind us. It’s just the first toward who Atlanta is and who Atlanta is going to be the next couple of years.” The post Angel Reese Answers With 30 Points and 16 Rebounds as the Atlanta Dream Win Their First Finals Game Ever appeared first on Where Is The Buzz | Breaking News, Entertainment, Exclusive Interviews & Morero .

item.title: The ‘goalie hugs’ were extra tight in Utah Monday night
item.description: Utah Mammoth goaltender Sebastian Cossa (33) gets a hug from Utah Mammoth defenseman Andrew Peeke (20) after the Utah Mammoth beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-4 in an NHL game at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. | Kristin Murphy, Deseret News One by one, Sebastian Cossa is checking his childhood dreams off his list. First NHL start? Check. First win? Check. First home game? Check. First times facing Connor McDavid and Sidney Crosby? Check and check. “Every game is a new experience and a new challenge, so it’s cool,” the 23-year-old said after helping the Utah Mammoth to a 5-4 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins Monday night. Cossa had his good and bad moments throughout the game — that’s the life of a hockey goalie — but none was bigger than his game-saving save on Ben Kindel with four seconds left on the clock. BIG save from Sebastian Cossa 🤩 pic.twitter.com/1UiIWLuYyC — Utah Mammoth (@utahmammoth) October 20, 2026 The first thought through his mind after making the save? “Is the game over yet?” Cossa smiled. “I think (Cossa) squeezed me pretty hard at the end of that one,” teased Utah defenseman Nate Schmidt, one of the defensemen responsible for covering Kindel in that instance. “But he deserves it. I might have to go get an oxygen tank.” Cossa hasn’t had a perfect start to his NHL career. His statistics don’t match those of the best goalies in the league. But in two of his three starts to this point, he has made the necessary saves to keep his team in the game. The same analysis can made of fellow Northern Alberta native Grant Fuhr throughout most of his career — and that’s the man Wayne Gretzky says is the greatest goalie of all time. There were plenty of games where Fuhr allowed four, five, even six goals, but if his team was protecting a narrow lead, he simply wouldn’t let another one in. The Mammoth won 5-4. | Kristin Murphy, Deseret News Mammoth head coach André Tourigny gave meaningful insight into Cossa’s development. “Like every young player who arrives in the league — it’s an expression (you’ve heard) before — the game has to slow down for him,” the coach said. “Right now, the game is probably fast for him and he gets surprised in some situations. “When we say that, that has nothing to do with your ability to play in (this) league. It’s the ability to relax, slow down, be comfortable.” Tourigny mentioned after morning skate Monday that he wants to get Cossa into a rhythm, giving him consistent, manageable starts to help him grow into a top goaltender. In the present, though, the team was glad to have him. “When we needed him, he was great tonight, and that’s the most important part for a young goalie,” Schmidt said. GOALIE HUGS>>> pic.twitter.com/McyxWvW6W0 — Utah Mammoth (@utahmammoth) October 20, 2026 Another bright young spot for the Utah Mammoth On both sides of the puck, Daniil But has been exactly what Utah has needed this season. He slotted in on the team’s top line in the preseason, often skating alongside Clayton Keller and Nick Schmaltz, where he had a two-point game. He got bumped to the fourth line to start the regular season, and he has been just as effective in that role. The 21-year-old has points in all four home games, and he probably still has a whole other level of offensive potential. Most impressive, however, is his defensive game. In both Monday’s game against the Penguins and last Thursday’s game against the Edmonton Oilers, the Mammoth coaching staff has trusted But to defend a one-goal lead in the dying minutes of the game, and in both cases, the opponent has had a generational superstar on the ice. Tourigny said it was an obvious decision in both games. “There was no way I would not trust them,” he said of the entire fourth line, which also includes Kevin Stenlund and Jack McBain. “... They did not do anything in that period or in that game for me to not trust them.” Tourigny has had confidence in But for some time now. “I said it many times about But. But is a ‘when’ player. He’s not an ‘if’ player. He’s a player who gets it, you know? “And it was the same last year. We told you many times last year how smart he is, how detailed he is, how structured he is, how much he understands the game. item.title: An Intro to New Orioles GM Jared Banner
item.description: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 23: A general view of a Baltimore Orioles logo in the stadium before the game between the Baltimore Orioles and the Boston Red Sox at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on August 23, 2020 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Evan Thompson The Baltimore Orioles made a front-office shakeup on Monday, bringing in assistant general manager of the Chicago Cubs, Jared Banner, to become the new general manager alongside President of Baseball Operations Mike Elias. Banner, who served as the Cubs’ assistant GM from 2024 to 2026, joined after Elias expressed a desire to add “fresh voices” to the front office. Banner’s arrival could mark the start of a transitionary period between who controls the club and where the team is slated to go after a disappointing 2026 season . Regardless, it signals that the Orioles want to move away from a single-voice approach to roster building toward a more democratic, tiered approach. Orioles President of Baseball Operations Mike Elias welcomes the media and VIPs to the new facility. The Baltimore Orioles unveiled their new Player Development Complex to the media on Monday, Feb. 9, 2026. The 47,700 square-foot facility includes indoor batting cages and infield, a biomechanics lab, new outdoor covered batting cages and more fan access areas. Main Image Credit: Mike Lang / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Who Is Jared Banner? Jared Banner isn’t a well-known figure outside front office circles in Major League Baseball, but he’s certainly not an unknown suit. Banner started his journey in 2007 after his baseball playing career ended, starting as a Boston Red Sox intern after a successful internship. He then became a scout under head scout Ray Fagnant, helping comb the team for prospects in the 2011 draft. That draft brought in notable names, including pitcher Matt Barnes, outfielder Jackie Bradley Jr., and a high school prospect named Mookie Betts. Jared Banner has been named our next General Manager. item.content:encoded: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 23: A general view of a Baltimore Orioles logo in the stadium before the game between the Baltimore Orioles and the Boston Red Sox at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on August 23, 2020 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Evan Thompson The Baltimore Orioles made a front-office shakeup on Monday, bringing in assistant general manager of the Chicago Cubs, Jared Banner, to become the new general manager alongside President of Baseball Operations Mike Elias. Banner, who served as the Cubs’ assistant GM from 2024 to 2026, joined after Elias expressed a desire to add “fresh voices” to the front office. Banner’s arrival could mark the start of a transitionary period between who controls the club and where the team is slated to go after a disappointing 2026 season . Regardless, it signals that the Orioles want to move away from a single-voice approach to roster building toward a more democratic, tiered approach. Orioles President of Baseball Operations Mike Elias welcomes the media and VIPs to the new facility. The Baltimore Orioles unveiled their new Player Development Complex to the media on Monday, Feb. 9, 2026. The 47,700 square-foot facility includes indoor batting cages and infield, a biomechanics lab, new outdoor covered batting cages and more fan access areas. Main Image Credit: Mike Lang / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Who Is Jared Banner? Jared Banner isn’t a well-known figure outside front office circles in Major League Baseball, but he’s certainly not an unknown suit. Banner started his journey in 2007 after his baseball playing career ended, starting as a Boston Red Sox intern after a successful internship. He then became a scout under head scout Ray Fagnant, helping comb the team for prospects in the 2011 draft. That draft brought in notable names, including pitcher Matt Barnes, outfielder Jackie Bradley Jr., and a high school prospect named Mookie Betts. Jared Banner has been named our next General Manager. Welcome to Birdland, Jared! https://t.co/eMxXVzfnoH — Baltimore Orioles (@Orioles) October 19, 2026 Then-executive Vice President Theo Epstein praised Banner’s work with Fagnant in the Northeast and his noted work ethic, which led to several roles focused on player development and farm system work. That work also led Banner to a stint with the New York Mets as their farm director, along with his mentor, Allard Baird. Between 2019 and 2024, Banner oversaw the development of Pete Alonso, Andres Gimenez, Francisco Alvarez, and other notable Mets prospects. His most notable stint came between 2021 and 2024, when he became Vice President of player development for the Cubs. He was instrumental in overseeing Pete Crow-Armstrong’s development after the 2021 trade that sent Javier Baez to the Mets. The Cubs also saw success in their farm system with Cade Horton, Matt Shaw, and Michael Busch. He left the position for the assistant GM slot, building the Cubs’ farm system to number two before the 2024 season. Jared Banner’s Direction Is Clear Banner comes to the Orioles at a time when they are struggling to see progress in their pitching development, but have rebuilt their farm system with top-of-the-line rotation prospects. In fact, ESPN’s Jeff Passan noted on Monday that Banner’s resume in player development ultimately led Baltimore to secure him for the spot. That move also reunites him with Alonso from the Mets. News: The Baltimore Orioles are hiring Jared Banner as general manager, sources tell ESPN. Banner, who was an assistant GM with the Cubs, joins Mike Elias in Baltimore’s leadership after nearly two decades working a range of executive jobs with the Cubs, Mets and Red Sox. — Jeff Passan (@JeffPassan) October 19, 2026 The Orioles have one of the youngest rosters in MLB, with plenty of young talent in Jackson Holliday, Gunnar Henderson, Samuel Basallo, and Colton Cowser. Behind the current roster is a deep prospect pool that includes three strong rotation pieces (Anthony Eyanson, Joseph Dzierwa, and Caden Hunter) and three potential outfielders (Eric Booth Jr., Ike Irish, and Enddy Azocar). It comes as the Orioles deal with numerous holes in their roster, especially in the outfield and rotation. Taylor Ward was traded midseason, Tyler O’Neill hasn’t lived up to his potential, and the Orioles have no dependable fourth outfielder. In the rotation, Shane Baz needs help as impending free agent Trevor Rogers and Kyle Bradish regressed in 2026. The bullpen isn’t faring any better either, with the closer-by-committee approach failing to lock down games. With Banner coming on and getting a larger say in player development and structure, that bodes well for the top prospects. Three of them are projected to make their debut in 2027, while two could get the call the next year. If their player development works too well, it does open up an interesting predicament. Could Banner Make Trades to Win Now? Given the Orioles’ deep prospect pool , teams could call and offer big names to rebuild their own farms. If the Orioles have a strong farm system that improves in 2027, could Banner buck the trend and sell prospects to win now? It’s unclear what the trade market will look like, given the uncertainty around the Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiations. Still, if pitchers like Logan Gilbert from the Seattle Mariners or Edward Cabrera from the Cubs come on the market, they might make a move. It depends on how fast a deal is done and how weak the free-agent market is, but it’s not out of the realm of possibility. The Last Word Banner’s hire marks a shift in the organization’s tone and approach going forward. The team wants to prioritize player development and hashing out the pieces they already have on the major league roster. Whether they feel like trading pieces they don’t really need or trading for franchise faces remains to be seen. What’s clear is that Mike Elias’s days as the franchise’s sole dictator are over. Main Photo Credit: Scott Taetsch/Getty Images

item.title: Roberto De Zerbi reveals how clear-the-air talks and Marbella bonding trip inspired Tottenham's vital first Premier League win
item.description: Manchester United v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Candid talks spark Spurs revival Tottenham’s difficult start to the campaign appears to have reached a turning point following a 3-1 victory over Coventry on Monday night. After a testing period that saw the North London club languishing at the bottom of the table, De Zerbi pointed toward a shift in psychological approach. The manager revealed that a candid squad meeting held prior to their resilient 1-1 draw at Manchester United laid the groundwork for their recent improvement in form and spirit. De Zerbi emphasized that tactical tweaks were secondary to the human element within the dressing room. “It’s important. The result is important but most important, two things. First one, we are able to realise we can win a game like other teams in the Premier League. The second thing, if we put [in] something from ourselves like we have done in the last two weeks. The day before Old Trafford we had a big meeting and spoke about the situation. We can’t accept and can’t move on if we don’t accept responsibility,” the Spurs manager revealed. Overcoming the robot mentality Overcoming the robot mentality De Zerbi took his squad on a warm-weather training camp to Marbella last week, aiming to strengthen team unity away from the pressures of their routine schedule. The manager emphasized that the getaway was crucial for fostering genuine camaraderie, explaining that spending quality time together off the pitch helps transform the squad into a close-knit, family-like collective. He believes that this emotional bond is essential when adversity strikes during competition. “This week has been important because we spend time together and want to be like a family. During the game if you have a problem and there is a tough situation you have to play for your friend and your brother, not like 11 robot players on the pitch," he said. The impact of returning leaders A significant factor in Tottenham's resurgence has been the return of key personnel from long-term injury layoffs. James Maddison made his first competitive start in 536 days, marking the occasion with a spectacular opening goal that reminded the home faithful of his creative quality. The evening was further bolstered by the emotional return of Dejan Kulusevski , who stepped onto the pitch for the first time since sustaining a serious knee injury in May 2025. De Zerbi was quick to praise the influence that both Maddison and Kulusevski have on the rest of the squad. Their technical ability on the ball is matched by their status as leaders within the camp. “They are different players. Different talent, different experience, different personality. With them in the dressing room there is another atmosphere," the manager stated. Crucial relief ahead of London derby Crucial relief ahead of London derby The win moves Tottenham up to 16th place, providing much-needed breathing room as they navigate a busy fixture schedule. That resolve will face an immediate, stern test this Saturday, when Spurs make the challenging cross-town journey to face London rivals Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

item.title: ‘Jayden Daniels’ Football IQ Is 0.0,’ ‘Awareness Is So Bad’ — NFL World Rips Commanders QB’s ‘Horrible’ Mistake vs. 49ers
item.description: ‘Jayden Daniels’ Football IQ Is 0.0,’ ‘Awareness Is So Bad’ — NFL World Rips Commanders QB's ‘Horrible’ Mistake vs. 49ers The Washington Commanders entered their Week 6 matchup on Monday hoping to get back on track after their disappointing tie with the New York Giants. However, Jayden Daniels and his men couldn’t bounce back and suffered another frustrating loss, falling 23-17 to the San Francisco 49ers. Daniels still posted solid passing numbers in the game. However, one of his questionable decisions in crucial moments left many in the NFL community frustrated with the quarterback. NFL World Questions Jayden Daniels’ Awareness After Bizarre Decision Against 49ers The Commanders squandered a chance to win in overtime last week when Daniels scrambled for no gain with no timeouts remaining, and Washington couldn’t get lined up quickly enough to spike the ball before the clock expired. Daniels made another questionable decision during Monday’s game against the 49ers. In the second quarter, Washington faced a fourth-down situation, but he inexplicably threw the ball out of bounds instead of attempting a pass to a receiver who might have kept the play alive. The decision, coupled with Daniels seemingly laughing after the play, quickly sparked frustration across the NFL community. Daniels also made another costly situational mistake on Washington’s final possession. With 16 seconds left, no timeouts and the Commanders at the 49ers’ 28-yard line, he was flagged for intentional grounding, triggering a 10-second runoff before he was sacked on the game’s final play. “Jayden Daniels makes a terrible decision throwing the ball away on 4th down. Two weeks in a row just clueless on managing the game. Stop grinning bro, lock in,” RotoBaller’s Frank Ammirante wrote . “Jayden Daniels football IQ is 0.0,” Fox Sports’ Chris Fallica wrote . “When Jayden Daniels make a decision like that, it makes you think he’s at fault for what happened against the Giants. Why are you throwing the ball away on fourth down?” Fox Sports Radio co-host Mark Gunnels said . SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “Throwing the ball away on 4th down. One week after turning a win into a tie by massively botching end of game. Jayden Daniels yikes,” analyst Warren Sharp wrote . The sequence also raised questions about whether Daniels fully recognized the down-and-distance situation. Washington entered the game with a disappointing 1-3-1 record, leaving the team with little room for further costly mistakes. That is why Daniels’ latest decision drew even more scrutiny, especially after last week’s overtime mishap. “This is crazy this man awareness is so bad this the second week in a row Jayden Daniels have done this. Man run for the first down would’ve got it easy. He acted like they had another down,” ex-NFL star Roddy White said . “Jayden Daniels throwing the ball out of bounds on 4th down after last week’s fiasco is a horrible horrible look,” one said. The Commanders will have a bye in Week 7 before returning to action against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night, November 1. Daniels will have an opportunity to bounce back during the break and address the decision-making issues. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Manchester City have a hidden defensive asset in Vitor Reis. He needs to get on the pitch
item.description: Manchester City have a hidden defensive asset in Vitor Reis. He needs to get on the pitch So far this season, Enzo Maresca has heavily relied upon Ruben Dias and Marc Guehi in the heart of Manchester City. Given their status as leaders in Enzo Maresca’s squad, that is an understandable decision by the City manager. However, there have been signs that Marc Guehi and Ruben Dias are showing signs of fatigue . Manchester City’s fixture list doesn’t ease up any time soon. You do feel that Maresca will now have to play Abdukodir Khusanov and Vitor Reis in the heart of Manchester City’s defence to give Dias and Guehi a rest. In the case of Vitor Reis, it does seem like it is time for him to begin to play a bigger role for his team. Vitor Reis is yet to be given an opportunity to impress at Manchester City this season. So far this season, Vitor Reis has made two appearances for Manchester City. He started Manchester City’s 5-0 Carabao Cup third-round win over Norwich City. He also came on for the final minute of Manchester City’s 4-1 win over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park. For now, Vitor Reis has had to be patient and wait for opportunities to play. First of all, it is understandable why Enzo Maresca has heavily relied upon Ruben Dias and Marc Guehi to begin this season. Maresca has wanted to establish his system with his team. Dias and Guehi are crucial to Manchester City’s process. Vitor Reis is only 20 and isn’t ready for a prominent role at City. However, Manchester City’s fixture list is gruelling and it does seem like it is time to give Abdukodir Khusanov and Vitor Reis an opportunity to play to allow Guehi and Dias the opportunity to rest. Vitor Reis showed during his loan spell with Girona in La Liga last season how good he can be. The Brazilian international was by far and away the best young centre-back in La Liga last season. So he is more than capable of stepping up and playing a role for Manchester City. He just needs an opportunity. That hasn’t arrived yet but you feel that it should. Vitor Reis will likely start in Manchester City’s fourth round Carabao Cup tie against Brighton next week. But he perhaps should be given an opportunity to start tonight against AEK Athens. Tonight could be the night to give Vitor Reis an opportunity to play from the start. Manchester City face AEK Athens tonight at the Etihad Stadium in their third UEFA Champions League league phase fixture. Enzo Maresca’s side do need to pick up three points tonight. However, the opportunity for Maresca to rotate his squad is also there tonight. Especially when you consider that City could be without five key players tonight. That is where an opportunity for Vitor Reis to start may arise. He could step in at centre-back or play at right-back to make a back three when City have possession. The expectation would be that Josko Gvardiol will start at left-back and drift forward as he has all season. Either way, there is an opportunity for Vitor Reis to start tonight against AE

He also came on for the final minute of Manchester City’s 4-1 win over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park. For now, Vitor Reis has had to be patient and wait for opportunities to play. First of all, it is understandable why Enzo Maresca has heavily relied upon Ruben Dias and Marc Guehi to begin this season. Maresca has wanted to establish his system with his team. Dias and Guehi are crucial to Manchester City’s process. Vitor Reis is only 20 and isn’t ready for a prominent role at City. However, Manchester City’s fixture list is gruelling and it does seem like it is time to give Abdukodir Khusanov and Vitor Reis an opportunity to play to allow Guehi and Dias the opportunity to rest. Vitor Reis showed during his loan spell with Girona in La Liga last season how good he can be. The Brazilian international was by far and away the best young centre-back in La Liga last season. So he is more than capable of stepping up and playing a role for Manchester City. He just needs an opportunity. That hasn’t arrived yet but you feel that it should. Vitor Reis will likely start in Manchester City’s fourth round Carabao Cup tie against Brighton next week. But he perhaps should be given an opportunity to start tonight against AEK Athens. Tonight could be the night to give Vitor Reis an opportunity to play from the start. Manchester City face AEK Athens tonight at the Etihad Stadium in their third UEFA Champions League league phase fixture. Enzo Maresca’s side do need to pick up three points tonight. However, the opportunity for Maresca to rotate his squad is also there tonight. Especially when you consider that City could be without five key players tonight. That is where an opportunity for Vitor Reis to start may arise. He could step in at centre-back or play at right-back to make a back three when City have possession. The expectation would be that Josko Gvardiol will start at left-back and drift forward as he has all season. Either way, there is an opportunity for Vitor Reis to start tonight against AEK Athens. It remains to be seen if it is an option that Enzo Maresca will use. Manchester City do have a quality defensive option in Vitor Reis to use to allow Enzo Maresca to rotate his centre-backs. As of yet, the young Brazilian centre-back has yet to play prominent minutes for City this season. The likelihood of that changing does seem real and perhaps tonight is the night that Vitor Reis is called upon to start making an impact for his team.

item.title: Brazil coach visits Säbener Straße for discussion on Bayern Munich player
item.description: (Photo by F. Gabke/FC Bayern via Getty Images) Bayern Munich youngster Maycon Cardozo could be on Brazil’s radar as he continues his development in Germany, with Brazil U-20 and U-23 head coach Paulo Victor Gomes recently visiting Säbener Straße. According to Bild (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Gomes met with Bayern head coach Vincent Kompany and club legend Dante during his visit. One of the reasons for the trip was Cardozo, as the Brazilian coach continues to monitor young Brazilian talents playing abroad. Cardozo is currently working his way back from shoulder surgery, meaning the youngster is focused on his recovery as he looks to get back on the pitch. Nevertheless, his progress at Bayern has evidently caught the attention of those responsible for identifying Brazil’s next generation of international talent. For Cardozo, the interest could be particularly meaningful. The youngster has repeatedly emphasized that representing Brazil’s national teams is a major personal ambition, making Gomes’ visit an encouraging development as he works toward that goal. There is no indication yet that a call-up is imminent, but the visit highlights the attention Cardozo is receiving as he continues his journey at Bayern. With Brazil keeping tabs on its emerging talents across Europe, Cardozo will hope to recover fully, return to action, and eventually turn his international dream into reality. Join the conversation! item.title: Jota delighted by his Paradise return
item.description: Jota delighted by his Paradise return Last week saw the return of Jota, with the Portuguese winger getting a superb emotional ovation from the entire away support as he entered the Fir Park pitch as a second half substitute in the 2-0 win over Motherwell… Jota of Celtic celebrates after the Scottish Premiership match between Motherwell and Celtic at Fir Park on October 11, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) It was a pivotal moment for the former Benfica player, as it was his first appearance at first team level in 18 months, and marked a significant milestone in his battle to full fitness. That was followed on Sunday afternoon when Celtic’s Superstar from Portugal got an even bigger reception from the moment he was sent out to warm up, with his appearance as a second half substitute bringing an even louder applause as he made his first appearance at Paradise in what must have felt like an eternity. The 27 year old spoke of his happiness at the reception he received, and was glad the supporters had a great day out as the hoops ran riot against the Jambos. Jota said: “It felt amazing. I was expecting this moment for a long time now, and I think it was a great day as well for everyone. We delivered, and I was really happy with it as well.” The Celtic favourite described each game as a “new story” and was grateful to have played in a match where the team was already comfortable. Post match, talking to Celtic TV, Jota expressed his determination to fully recover and regain the sensations that come with regular play. He said: “It’s good to hear. It’s good that people can see that as well. I feel very good as well. I feel fresh. “Obviously, there’s a process to it, but I’m just thrilled to be playing minutes after minutes and just get all of the sensations back again.” “I still want to achieve a lot of stuff with them, and I just can’t wait to get back to the level and just deliver every game.” Speaking to the mainstream media Jota continued with this theme. “It’s like a rollercoaster of emotions,” Jota said via Newsquest’s TCW , as he reflected on the time out of the game through that ACL injury picked up at Tannadice early in April 2025. “We could stay here for like two weeks for me to speak about everything that was going on in my head. Like, what can I say? I mean in the end, it’s part of everyone’s life. Everyone struggles. The thing is that in our job, I just cannot be out there. “But certainly other people, and I always try to see from this perspective, like they have worse problems. I always think there’s someone in a worse position than you. “So I’m just grateful to – and I think I’m privileged to – be in such a wonderful sport and to have all of these experiences. Today it shows that it matters, like all of the struggle. It matters because these moments are unique.” The longer Jota was out the more supporters started to worry that he may never recover properly from the injury, effectively ending his playing career. Not so Jota himself. “

That was followed on Sunday afternoon when Celtic’s Superstar from Portugal got an even bigger reception from the moment he was sent out to warm up, with his appearance as a second half substitute bringing an even louder applause as he made his first appearance at Paradise in what must have felt like an eternity. The 27 year old spoke of his happiness at the reception he received, and was glad the supporters had a great day out as the hoops ran riot against the Jambos. Jota said: “It felt amazing. It’s good that people can see that as well. I feel very good as well. I feel fresh. “Obviously, there’s a process to it, but I’m just thrilled to be playing minutes after minutes and just get all of the sensations back again.” “I still want to achieve a lot of stuff with them, and I just can’t wait to get back to the level and just deliver every game.” Speaking to the mainstream media Jota continued with this theme. “It’s like a rollercoaster of emotions,” Jota said via Newsquest’s TCW , as he reflected on the time out of the game through that ACL injury picked up at Tannadice early in April 2025. “We could stay here for like two weeks for me to speak about everything that was going on in my head. Like, what can I say? I mean in the end, it’s part of everyone’s life. Everyone struggles. The thing is that in our job, I just cannot be out there. “But certainly other people, and I always try to see from this perspective, like they have worse problems. I always think there’s someone in a worse position than you. “So I’m just grateful to – and I think I’m privileged to – be in such a wonderful sport and to have all of these experiences. Today it shows that it matters, like all of the struggle. It matters because these moments are unique.” The longer Jota was out the more supporters started to worry that he may never recover properly from the injury, effectively ending his playing career. Not so Jota himself. “Oh, come on,” Jota said. “No, obviously this is my dream. It’s my passion. I was always being fuelled by this. “So there are moments where you reflect, there are moments where you feel like you’re down and you cannot see any light, but that doesn’t mean that you stop believing. “You just need to find another way. And that’s what I was trying to do all the time. And every case is different. My situation is not the same situation as another player. But in the end, my aim was always like I want to come back fit. “Whatever time I need to take, because I still have a long career in front of me and I’m still young. So there’s no rush, let’s do everything correctly and just trust the process.” His love of playing football also helped Jota through this dark months out of the game and that set a course for his return to Paradise on Sunday afternoon. “Just the passion for football. I think that’s my compass. I could clearly see that during the months I was away. And my love for football is immense. I could prove that because maybe someone else wouldn’t want to come back because of the struggle or like some guys just don’t have that on themselves. “I think that was my fuel to keep on working every day, to be healthy and fit, even if things weren’t going that way. But there’s a solution for everything. You just need to accept the present and keep on believing that good things will come.” Jota admitted that he found in hard watching games due to his own injury woes. “It’s very painful because you want to be there inside and help them and you can’t and you don’t know when you will be again. So again, you just need to rewire inside and see the positives.”

item.title: Sharks Locker Room: Celebrini Staying Positive, Askarov on “Better” Performance, Warsofsky Discloses Wennberg Injury
item.description: TORONTO — The San Jose Sharks, on one hand, have played some of their best 5-on-5 hockey this season over the last five games. On the other hand, they’re 1-3-1 to show for it. That trend continued in the San Jose Sharks’ 3-1 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs on Monday. Mason Marchment scored the lone goal and Yaroslav Askarov turned away 28-of-30 shots. According to Natural Stat Trick, the Sharks outchanced the Leafs at High-Danger 14-6 at 5-on-5. But they were felled by special teams, surrendering two power play goals and scoring none. Macklin Celebrini said the Sharks aren’t playing “bad hockey”, Askarov discussed his game, Marchment talked about Tyler Toffoli , and Ryan Warsofsky gave an Alex Wennberg injury update. A deeper game story with micro-stats from Stathletes and game action clips, Sharks Insight, will be published soon. Mason Marchment Marchment, on Tyler Toffoli’s pass on his goal: I just saw him keeping it in. I just tried to stay under him and he made a great play through everyone. It was just a quick move. Marchment, on the San Jose Sharks power play’s struggles to enter the zone: There’s definitely some execution. They’re holding the line really strong. Sometimes, it can make it hard, but again, we just got to make better plays. Macklin Celebrini Celebrini, on recent #SJSharks play: "We're not playing bad hockey. We're losing one-goal games, aside from that Boston game, where we still created a lot and probably deserved better. We're in all these games, and it's just the little stuff, the details that have cost us games… — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) October 20, 2026 Celebrini, on the Sharks power play’s struggles to enter the zone: It’s just sloppy. Miscommunications. Weren’t really on the same page. I think it’s gonna happen, but we gotta be better and work through it and talk to each other. Celebrini, on if this has been a season-long issue: I don’t think so. Like we’ve had some amazing power plays this year, where we’re getting a lot of chances and had really good chemistry. It’s just tonight was a little off. View this post on Instagram Yaroslav Askarov View this post on Instagram Ryan Warsofsky Warsofsky, on Toffoli this season: He’s been really good. A very experienced veteran. Understands what’s going on in the game, his leadership, and then his play. He’s trying to play within our system, and he does a good job of that and understanding the game within the game. Warsofsky, on Sam Dickinson’s recent play: We’re seeing a big jump here in his development, in his stacking games, so that’s a good thing. Warsofsky, on the San Jose Sharks’ power play entries: Our power play entries this year, analytically speaking, are pretty high. I don’t think that has been an issue for the most part. Tonight, it was an issue. Wennberg upper-body injury, left in middle of 3rd and didn’t finish game. So in question tomorrow — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) October 20, 2026 Related Headlines Askarov Bounces Back, But Sharks Fall 3-1 to Maple Leafs McKenn

item.title: Euro giants ready to pounce for disillusioned Man Utd talisman who’s out of contract at the end of the season
item.description: Euro giants ready to pounce for disillusioned Man Utd talisman who’s out of contract at the end of the season Galatasaray have reportedly set their sights on a move for Bruno Fernandes ahead of his contract expiring at the end of the season. As things stand, Manchester United do hold the option of extending his stay by an additional 12 months, which they will likely do in order to avoid him leaving for nothing. Bruno Fernandes: The state of play (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Turkish outlet Fanatik claims that Fernandes has grown disillusioned with his Red Devils future. Fernandes’ complete record in all competitions for MUFC He has previously outlined on numerous occasions how he wants to see the side back competing for the biggest honours in club football, yet United are once again on track to be battling it out for a European place and have already exited one competition, the Carabao Cup, at the earliest stage. It’s said that the United skipper privately agreed with Lisandro Martinez’s post-match comments in Madrid last Tuesday, during which the defender voiced his disappointment with the board’s lack of investment over the summer window. Will Fernandes decide to pull the curtains on his United tenure? (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Reports have also suggested that Fernandes’ contract talks have now reached an impasse , with United actively working to have him agree to an extension so that his long-term future is secure at Old Trafford. Fans have pointed out that the Portugal star does seem to be cutting a more frustrated and exasperated figure than usual, and Sunday’s stalemate at Elland Road marked a fifth consecutive game without a goal contribution for Fernandes. Bruno Fernandes looking very angry after Tottenham's game [@TheEyeTest_1] pic.twitter.com/5RVPJ8CMOF It remains to be seen where he would look to ply his trade next, and whether the Super Lig giants could tempt him into a move abroad to play alongside the likes of Ilkay Gundogan, Victor Osimhen and compatriot Rafael Leao. Is Bruno Fernandes 'fed up'? 😳 pic.twitter.com/N1wRSIQHLb Share Tweet Share Share Email Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. item.title: 3 Guardians to blame for painful ALCS Game 6 loss to World Series-bound Rays
item.description: Cade Smith, Stephen Vogt and Shawn Armstrong. 3 Guardians to blame for painful ALCS Game 6 loss to World Series-bound Rays appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 World Series is set after Game 6 of the ALCS ended in a 7-3 Tampa Bay Rays series-clinching win that led to a cold-blood take from Cleveland Guardians manager Stephen Vogt. The Guardians started a surprising player in Game 6, reliever Shawn Armstrong , but he didn’t pitch the way the team hoped as they fell behind the eight-ball early at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. Now that the smoke has cleared on one of the most painful losses in recent Cleveland Guardians history, it’s time to assign blame. The Guardians bowed out of the playoffs in the ALCS for the second time in three years, and still have not won a World Series title since way back in 1948. It’s going to take a better effort in 2027 to make it back to the team’s first World Series since 2016, but for now, fans are wondering exactly where it all went wrong, and who deserves the blame for the latest tough-luck series loss. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Guardian #1: Stephen Vogt David Richard-Imagn Images Vogt is an up-and-comer among MLB managers with a lot of baseball knowledge to spread among his team, but he appeared outfoxed in the clinching Game 6, particularly in terms of his pitching rotation. The Guardians were caught flat-footed and without an inspiring plan during the final matchup at Tropicana Field, as they trotted eight different pitchers out to the mound and gave up seven runs in a losing effort. The Rays also used a lot of pitchers, six to be exact, but something felt haphazard about Vogt’s strategy as Armstrong exited the game with one runner stranded and Tim Herrin allowed a base hit making the score 2-0 in favor of the Rays. Vogt got the Guardians to the ALCS based on his smart managing throughout the season, but it was hard not to feel like he was outfoxed by Rays manager Kevin Cash in this one as Cleveland felt off-balance throughout the night in a painful Game 6 loss fans will remember for many years to come. The Guardians’ defense had its moments during the series, but the pitching and offense ultimately let down Vogt’s team in another hard-luck loss in the American League playoffs. Guardian #2: Shawn Armstrong Armstrong was thrust into a difficult situation as the Guardians’ starter in a do-or-die Game 6 in St. Petersburg. He failed to make the most of the opportunity as he exited with a stat line of one inning pitched, one hit given up and one earned run. Armstrong’s appearance was perhaps more of an indictment on the Guardians’ staff as a whole, and of Vogt, in that there were no better options to start off the game from Cleveland’s starting pitching staff. item.content:encoded: Cade Smith, Stephen Vogt and Shawn Armstrong. 3 Guardians to blame for painful ALCS Game 6 loss to World Series-bound Rays appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 World Series is set after Game 6 of the ALCS ended in a 7-3 Tampa Bay Rays series-clinching win that led to a cold-blood take from Cleveland Guardians manager Stephen Vogt. The Guardians started a surprising player in Game 6, reliever Shawn Armstrong , but he didn’t pitch the way the team hoped as they fell behind the eight-ball early at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. Now that the smoke has cleared on one of the most painful losses in recent Cleveland Guardians history, it’s time to assign blame. The Guardians bowed out of the playoffs in the ALCS for the second time in three years, and still have not won a World Series title since way back in 1948. It’s going to take a better effort in 2027 to make it back to the team’s first World Series since 2016, but for now, fans are wondering exactly where it all went wrong, and who deserves the blame for the latest tough-luck series loss. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Guardian #1: Stephen Vogt David Richard-Imagn Images Vogt is an up-and-comer among MLB managers with a lot of baseball knowledge to spread among his team, but he appeared outfoxed in the clinching Game 6, particularly in terms of his pitching rotation. The Guardians were caught flat-footed and without an inspiring plan during the final matchup at Tropicana Field, as they trotted eight different pitchers out to the mound and gave up seven runs in a losing effort. The Rays also used a lot of pitchers, six to be exact, but something felt haphazard about Vogt’s strategy as Armstrong exited the game with one runner stranded and Tim Herrin allowed a base hit making the score 2-0 in favor of the Rays. Vogt got the Guardians to the ALCS based on his smart managing throughout the season, but it was hard not to feel like he was outfoxed by Rays manager Kevin Cash in this one as Cleveland felt off-balance throughout the night in a painful Game 6 loss fans will remember for many years to come. The Guardians’ defense had its moments during the series, but the pitching and offense ultimately let down Vogt’s team in another hard-luck loss in the American League playoffs. Guardian #2: Shawn Armstrong Armstrong was thrust into a difficult situation as the Guardians’ starter in a do-or-die Game 6 in St. Petersburg. He failed to make the most of the opportunity as he exited with a stat line of one inning pitched, one hit given up and one earned run. Armstrong’s appearance was perhaps more of an indictment on the Guardians’ staff as a whole, and of Vogt, in that there were no better options to start off the game from Cleveland’s starting pitching staff. Typically, teams will throw out their best starting arms in a do-or-die games such as October 20’s, but Vogt didn’t do it against a Rays team that looked ready and willing to jump all over Cleveland pitching from the start of the game. Vogt sensed this dynamic and continued to try different bullpen arms throughout the night, but the Rays eventually broke free as they pushed across run-after-run late in the game to secure the victory. Armstrong didn’t have a large sample size to draw from in this game and didn’t have much time to settle in, but he also didn’t quite perform the way Vogt envisioned when he chose him to lead things off. Guardian #3: Cade Smith Smith gave up a two-run home run to Junior Caminero in the bottom of the seventh inning that broke the game wide open for Cash’s team, extending the Rays’ lead to 5-1. Smith finished with a stat line of one inning pitched, one hit given up, two earned runs, and one walk with zero strikeouts, a disappointing way for the Guardians pitcher to end a season that saw him thrive with a 1.95 ERA and a 6-1 record as a reliever. The Caminero homer showed that it simply wasn’t the Guardians’ night as he rocked one of Vogt’s better pitchers, putting an exclamation mark on a magical night for the Rays in St. Petersburg. Vogt’s Guardians gave up seven hits on the night, leading to the Rays’ seven runs, an outcome made possible by an uncharacteristic six walks given up by Cleveland pitching. Guardians pitchers finished with just three strikeouts on the night, an indication that the Rays simply didn’t fear the long list of hurlers Vogt paraded out on a disappointing night in West-Central Florida. The 2026 Guardians season is officially in the books, and it was another exciting, albeit disappointing, one for Vogt’s team. As the team gets ready to turn the page toward another hot-stove winter and what should be another eventful offseason, it’s hard not to feel like Cleveland fans were cheated, and let down in a roundabout way. 2027 could bring brighter October days and perhaps another World Series appearance, but for now, fans are justifiably going through a gamut of emotions as they try to make sense of a season that ended in a dramatic “thud” against a Rays team that appeared as if it simply wanted to win more than the Guardians did. Related: Guardians’ Stephen Vogt gives props to Cleveland’s pitchers for stepping up in Game 6 Related: Guardians’ Stephen Vogt delivers cold-blooded message to players after painful ALCS exit

Not even the immensely friendly and polite Salt Lake City denizens showed the Penguins hospitality as the Penguins finished their four-game road trip sans a point, and didn’t come close. The Penguins were competitive early Monday but slid further and further behind, eventually losing 5-4 to the Utah Mammoth at the Delta Center. The Penguins gave up 21 goals on the four-game trip and scored just 11. Only the Vancouver Canucks (45) have given up more goals this season than the Penguins (38). But it’s still a young season … and the Penguins could easily catch Vancouver with a few more games. Yes, the scoreboard showed a close game, and yes, the Penguins were a puck pounce in the final seconds away from tying the game as Ben Kindel slammed a pouncing puck into Utah goalie Sebastian Cossa; had Kindel not got the puck first, it was headed toward Sidney Crosby on the side of the crease, and Crosby would have had a wide open net. “Yeah,” lamented Crosby. A pair of quick power play goals kept them in the game early, and a couple of quick strikes late made the contest competitive. But the Penguins were bad again. Nay, they were terrible. Again. item.content:encoded: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect SALT LAKE CITY — Pittsburgh Penguins coach Dan Muse emerged from the Penguins locker room with an intense stare following his team’s 5-4 loss to the Utah Mammoth at the Delta Center Monday. Not even the immensely friendly and polite Salt Lake City denizens showed the Penguins hospitality as the Penguins finished their four-game road trip sans a point, and didn’t come close. The Penguins were competitive early Monday but slid further and further behind, eventually losing 5-4 to the Utah Mammoth at the Delta Center. The Penguins gave up 21 goals on the four-game trip and scored just 11. Only the Vancouver Canucks (45) have given up more goals this season than the Penguins (38). But it’s still a young season … and the Penguins could easily catch Vancouver with a few more games. Yes, the scoreboard showed a close game, and yes, the Penguins were a puck pounce in the final seconds away from tying the game as Ben Kindel slammed a pouncing puck into Utah goalie Sebastian Cossa; had Kindel not got the puck first, it was headed toward Sidney Crosby on the side of the crease, and Crosby would have had a wide open net. “Yeah,” lamented Crosby. And that about sums up the last two weeks. At no point did the Penguins control the game or exert anything resembling overwhelming pressure. A pair of quick power play goals kept them in the game early, and a couple of quick strikes late made the contest competitive. But the Penguins were bad again. Nay, they were terrible. Again. Muse returned a few minutes later into the well-lit Delta Center hallway as equipment and medical carts wheeled past as the Penguins prepared to fly home Tuesday. Muse returned to face the media, and pressed against a painted black concrete wall, his exasperation was controlled but audibly present. The Penguins coach looked every bit like a bench boss who deep down knows the answer, but can’t begin to verbalize that his team is full of talent but is horribly mismatched for the roles they need. The Penguins have a lot of players who are not good defensively, and unfortunately, it appears some of those players are defensemen, such as Declan Carlile , who continues to be a problem. “I think it’s that we have to be tighter. We have to. I mean, you see bodies in the area. We’ve got to make sure that we’re eliminating options. So, it’s the details on the defensive side. We have to keep looking at it,” said Muse. “If you look at the game, the second half of the game we got a little bit better with it, but the consistency is not there right now. We have to continue to make that a priority within our game. (On) the defensive side, being harder to play against, and again, I’m putting that on all of us, myself included. “Like that has to be there, and it has to be a priority. We have to make sure that we’re taking steps because right now, if you look at the chances that are given up, like, there’s not a lot that our goalies can do.” The Penguins coach has every reason to feel befuddled and dazed. His steam stinks right now. Their defensive zone coverage could reasonably be declared a disaster area, and the Penguins’ only consistency is their ability to badly botch D-zone assignments. It’s every line, every defense pairing, though some bear far more culpability than others. “You look at the chances that we’re giving up. Are they the exact same? No. But I think it’s just the attention on the defensive side, details, the returns, making sure that we’re all on the same page in regard to the structure,” Muse said. “All those things factor in, and so it’s a number of them, and it’s about being consistent with the way that we play away from the puck and on the defensive side.” Following his obligatory questions from the media scrum, Muse paced the Delta Center hallway looking like a coach trying to find answers but knowing deep down there are none, or at least none that can be addressed at the coaching level. Penguins goalie Arturs Silovs was a controlled impulse away from absolutely lambasting his team, which again hung him out to dry. No one summed up the team’s repetitive defensive gaffes with more precision and disgust. Silovs stopped 24 of 29 shots, which is ordinarily a bad night for the goalie. Indeed, Silovs didn’t have a good night, but it wasn’t due to his own struggles. This season, Silovs has merely an .866 save percentage, but the numbers have no correlation to his game. “I felt like I played good [sic]. I think they won some net-front battles in front of the net, and they scored some greasy ones,” Silovs said. “You know we (have to) try to keep battling.” Indeed, Utah swarmed him in the first period, especially. ‘Well, they create a lot of odd-man rushes. I think, especially in the first period, I felt like they would just keep coming, keep coming towards us, and I was just trying to lock it down and play as good for my teammates, as good I can.” The Penguins had a little shake and bake in the opening minutes. Erik Karlsson scored a power-play goal. He and Spencer Stastney were working well together at 5v5, and the Penguins were pushing the puck. But their advantage was ever so brief before Utah soaked them for two unanswered goals twice, and a 4-2 lead after 40 minutes. Not only did Utah surge ahead, but they largely dominated the game. The shots were 25-13 for Utah by the end of the second, and the Penguins’ offensive zone pressure was faster than a run down the local bobsled track. The Penguins had a puncher’s chance in the end, but even then they didn’t hem Utah into their zone until the final few minutes. Penguins Report Card Team: C- The Penguins avoided another F with a passable third period in which they buried a couple of chances. Their game lacks details, fundamentals, and sometimes effort. “We’ve been feeding the other team’s transition too much with the turnovers throughout the whole game,” said Rakell. “It’s mostly in our own zone and the neutral zone.” Penguins Best Players Erik Karlsson: B The Penguins blue liner would be the first to admit he misplayed Nick Schmaltz’s goal, which became the game winner. However, Karlsson also had his legs Monday. He pushed the play and held onto the puck. He led the team with one goal, one assist, eight shot attempts, and was generally visible in the positive. Arturs Silovs: B+ He was very good and gave the team a chance to win. Perhaps if the Penguins don’t want to see a five or six spot on the scoreboard, they might consider preventing opponents from bearing down on Silovs unabated or uncovered at the net. Silov momentarily flashed that anger that only goalies understand; goalies who bear the brunt but don’t deserve it. Rickard Rakell: B+ After a snake-bitten beginning to the season, he finished his chance and connected with Crosby. Kris Letang: Solid The Penguins defenseman skated with recalled Ilya Solovyov and was solid Monday. Letang led the team with three shots on goal and played a clean game. Not the Best Declan Carlile: It just seems the Penguins defenseman is in the eye of the storm. Mistakes and gaffes, the puck is chasing him. After a nice start in camp and preseason, Carlile has been precarious. Monday he was beaten by Kevin Stenland at the net front and was later shed by a rusher, setting up a bang-bang goal. Muse paired him with Kaedan Korczak Monday instead of Karlsson. Other players who were too quiet Monday were Nick Robertson, Andrei Kuzmenko, and Ville Koivunen. Related Headlines Penguins Somehow Keep Close, but Lose; Breaking Down the Goals Penguins Game 10, Clean Up: Lines, Goalies, & How to Watch vs. Mammoth (UPDATED) Updated: Penguins Demote Johnson, Recall D Read more at Pittsburgh Hockey Now

item.title: Sabres’ Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen Trade Could Decide Connor Hellebuyck Landing Spot
item.description: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen Sabres Getty The Buffalo Sabres remain heavily in the trade rumors for Connor Hellebuyck. At this point, it’s not even clear what’s real on social media and what isn’t but one aspect is quite obvious: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen matters here. Over the summer, it seemed the Sabres could end up trading UPL to the Winnipeg Jets in a deal for Hellebuyck. The latest suggestions instead make it look like it’d be a three-team deal where Luukkonen goes somewhere else. There’s definitely plenty of reason to believe that a Hellebuyck trade would somehow involve a Luukkonen move, one way or another. Jets Might Not Need Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen The first aspect to consider here is that the Jets no longer seem to need UPL as much. At least with how they’ve begun the season, Winnipeg likely believes they have two usable goalies for this season. Stuart Skinner is the veteran who is playing well in the early going. Then they picked up Clay Stevenson off waivers, and he’s performing at the best level he’s ever shown professionally. It seemed straightforward that trading away Hellebuyck would bring back a goalie to Winnipeg, but that’s no longer as clear. UPL might not be able to find a new home with the Jets. UPL’s Logical Landing Spot There’s one spot that makes more sense for Luukkonen to end up: the New York Rangers . The Rangers lost Igor Shesterkin to a season-ending injury, and they still are without Joonas Korpisalo due to injury. That leaves Dylan Garand getting as much action as he can handle. The rest of the Rangers’ possible options are guys that they would probably prefer to have in the AHL. Luukkonen would be some level of upgrade, and he could probably push for the starting gig as things stand. The social media rumors suggest that it’s the Rangers portion of proceedings that isn’t going well so far. It’s hard to know what to believe, but it’s fair to think that’s true. The Rangers would know why Buffalo wants to trade Luukkonen, which would remove a lot of the Sabres’ leverage. New York would likely not offer a ton, and so Buffalo would have to decide what to do. But the reality is also this — if the Sabres can end up with Hellebuyck, it feels like a move worth making no matter what the other tendrils in a potential three-team deal might be. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Sabres’ Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen Trade Could Decide Connor Hellebuyck Landing Spot appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Commanders’ Dan Quinn Goes Viral for What He Said During 49ers Game
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Dan Quinn of the Washington Commanders looks on from sidelines against the Philadelphia Eagles in the third quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty The Washington Commanders entered Monday night’s showdown against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers looking to bounce back from their Week 5 result. Instead, they did just about the opposite in the first half. They trailed 20-3 at the break and had several viral moments across the first two quarters, all for the wrong reasons. Daniels Makes Costly Mistake One of the biggest mistakes in the first half came from quarterback Jayden Daniels, who elected to throw the football out of bounds on a fourth-and-2 play in the red zone. Instead of keeping the ball in play and giving his wide receivers a chance to make a play, draw a penalty or score a touchdown from inside the 20-yard line, Daniels threw the ball into the stands beyond the back of the end zone. To make matters worse, a clip of Commanders head coach Dan Quinn went viral on social media after fans tried to read his lips following the play. Some viewers interpreted his reaction as a sign that he didn’t even realize it was fourth down. Check it out: “Field goal. Oh, that was 4th down?” certainly looks like lip readers believe Dan Quinn was completely unaware that it was 4th down and wanted to kick a field goal 💀💀💀 https://t.co/yJYuAUmVZX — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) October 20, 2026 The video, posted by Warren Sharp , surpassed 250,000 views in less than an hour. The clip also spread across several X posts, with fans questioning how Quinn seemingly didn’t know the Commanders were going for it on fourth down. Fans React on Social Media “I don’t root for anybody to lose their job but,” one fan wrote. Someone else added, “the QB not knowing the down either is just as bad.” “That’s what I saw. Seems very odd. No way you can let him continue with the organization,” another person wrote. “Last week a field goal would have won it and now he’s asking if it’s 4th down. This team is cooked,” a fan shared. One more person commented, “f Quinn is still the coach this week, regardless of result, it’s malpractice by the ownership.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Commanders’ Dan Quinn Goes Viral for What He Said During 49ers Game appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Philadelphia 76ers Get LeBron James News Before Knicks Season Opener
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 16: LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers looks on prior to the preseason game against the Boston Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 16, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 16: LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers tosses chalk in the air prior to the preseason game against the Boston Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 16, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Celtics defeated the 76ers 125-120 in overtime. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty The Philadelphia 76ers appear ready to unleash LeBron James when the 2026-27 NBA regular season begins Tuesday, October 20. James is not listed on Philadelphia’s first official injury report ahead of its opening-night matchup against the defending champion New York Knicks. That means the 41-year-old superstar is expected to play and start in his first regular-season game with the Sixers, barring a late setback. It’s a welcome development for Philadelphia, which listed six other players on Monday’s injury report, including three who have already been ruled out. For James, Tuesday’s game represents another milestone in a career already filled with them. He is set to become the first player in NBA history to appear in a 24th season. Is LeBron James Playing Against the Knicks? Yes, James is expected to play against New York on October 20 after avoiding an injury designation on Monday. He is also projected to start alongside Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, V.J. Edgecombe and Joel Embiid, giving Philadelphia one of the NBA’s most star-studded starting lineups. James’ availability is particularly encouraging following a carefully managed preseason. The four-time NBA champion dealt with chronic arthritis in his left foot entering training camp, according to ESPN’s Dave McMenamin. Sixers coach Nick Nurse also indicated that the team intended to manage James’ workload throughout the season. James made his preseason debut against the Brooklyn Nets on October 8, recording 10 points, five assists and four rebounds in 18 minutes. He attempted only one field goal but converted all eight of his free throws. Now, the Sixers appear prepared to move forward with James in the lineup when the games begin to count. Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – OCTOBER 16: LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers tosses chalk in the air prior to the preseason game against the Boston Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 16, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Celtics defeated the 76ers 125-120 in overtime. NOTE
