James made his preseason debut against the Brooklyn Nets on October 8, recording 10 points, five assists and four rebounds in 18 minutes. He attempted only one field goal but converted all eight of his free throws. Now, the Sixers appear prepared to move forward with James in the lineup when the games begin to count. Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – OCTOBER 16: LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers tosses chalk in the air prior to the preseason game against the Boston Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 16, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Celtics defeated the 76ers 125-120 in overtime. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) LeBron James’ Historic Numbers Entering His 24th NBA Season James may be entering his age-41 season, but his production with the Los Angeles Lakers last year demonstrated that he remains capable of making a substantial impact. In 60 games during the 2025-26 campaign, James averaged 20.9 points, 7.2 assists and 6.1 rebounds. He also earned All-NBA Second Team honors. Those numbers were below his extraordinary career averages, but they would still represent valuable production for a Philadelphia team featuring several established scorers. His history in season openers offers another reason for optimism. According to NBA.com, James has averaged 24.3 points, 7.9 rebounds and 6.5 assists across his previous 23 opening-night appearances, shooting 50.2% from the field. He has scored at least 30 points in six of those games and recorded 11 double-doubles. His first NBA game, against the Sacramento Kings on October 29, 2003, featured 25 points, nine assists, six rebounds and four steals. More than two decades later, James will begin another season wearing a new uniform and pursuing a fifth NBA championship. 76ers Face Injury Questions Despite LeBron James’ Availability James’ expected availability does not mean Philadelphia will be at full strength against New York. The Sixers ruled out Dominick Barlow, Tacko Fall and Ariel Hukporti on Monday. Anfernee Simons, Adem Bona and Dean Wade were listed as questionable. Those absences could create immediate problems for Philadelphia’s frontcourt depth, even with Embiid also absent from the injury report. Simons’ status is another notable concern. The veteran guard missed the entire preseason with hamstring soreness, leaving his availability uncertain heading into opening night. Still, Philadelphia’s projected starting five remains intact. That presents an intriguing challenge for Nurse, who must find a way to balance James’ playmaking with the scoring abilities of Maxey, Brown and Embiid. Speaking to The Philadelphia Inquirer ahead of the opener, Nurse acknowledged the uncertainty surrounding how the new group will function together while expressing optimism about the team’s health. The Sixers will get their first meaningful test against a Knicks team preparing to celebrate its 2025-26 NBA championship. Philadelphia and New York tip off Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET at Madison Square Garden. The game will air on NBC and stream on Peacock. item.title: Alex Volkanovski Impressed by Rising UFC Star Kevin Vallejos
item.description: Kevin Vallejos Alexander Volkanovski UFC Getty UFC featherweight champion Alex Volkanovski says that he has been very impressed by rising young star Kevin Vallejos. Just 24 years of age, Vallejos is a top featherweight prospect out of Argentina who is already 4-0 in the UFC since joining the promotion just last year. He previously competed twice on Dana White’s Contender Series, losing a decision to Jean Silva in 2023 and then earning a UFC contract with a knockout win over Cam Teague in 2024. Next month at UFC Qatar, Vallejos gets the biggest fight of his life when he battles former UFC bantamweight champion Aljamain Sterling in a fight that could propel him to the featherweight division’s elite. Kevin Vallejos Impressing Alex Volkanovski Speaking to MMAjunkie.com ahead of his upcoming UFC featherweight title defense against Movsar Evloev at UFC 333, Volkanovski heaped praise upon Vallejos for what he’s done so far during his short career inside the Octagon. “After Movsar, you’ve got your Jean Silvas, you’ve got your Aljamain (Sterlings), who are both pretty much in the exact same position. They’re the ones who stand out the most right now. … That’s another one – (Kevin Vallejos) there. So whether Kevin can get a title fight that quick and jump the line, I don’t know,” Volkanovski said. “At the same time, Aljamain and Silva, they’re probably closest. But Kevin, he’s definitely someone – this is a test for him. You see a lot of guys who look good until they fight a veteran with fight IQ that’s calculated. Kevin is going to have a tough one here, but if he proves himself, he’s going to show that he deserves to be at the top.” Who Will Get the Next Featherweight Title Shot? Most likely, the next man in line for Volkanovski — should he get past Evloev this weekend — will be Silva, but Vallejos could very well steal the next title shot with an impressive win against Sterling. If Vallejos can go into Qatar and finish Sterling, it would go a long way towards cementing himself as the next UFC featherweight title challenger, though Sterling will do his best to make sure that doesn’t happen. item.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan shares Christian Kirk, Demarcus Robinson updates after MNF win
item.description: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan shares Christian Kirk, Demarcus Robinson updates after MNF win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers kept their undefeated season alive on Monday night, but it came at a steep cost. Already dealing with a ton of injuries in their wide receiver room, their star wide receiver exited the game with an injury. Veteran wideout Mike Evans exited the game with an Achilles injury. San Francisco was able to manage without their wide receiver for the game, but their situation suddenly looks more dire now. After the game, head coach Kyle Shanahan shared an update on the other 49ers’ injured wide receivers. In particular, Shanahan talked about Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson . Here’s what the head coach had to say about his two receivers. “Kyle Shanahan said Christian Kirk is a possibility to play next week, but he doesn’t think Demarcus Robinson will be ready to come off of IR,” Matt Barrows reported on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 49ers started this season with high expectations for their offense. After acquiring Evans in a trade this offseason, they had a solid wide receiver group. Evans joined a group that had Ricky Pearsall, Christian Kirk, and an exciting rookie in De’Zhaun Stribling. However, one by one, San Francisco’s 49ers dropped due to injuries. Kirk was ruled out early in the offseason due to an injury. Pearsall underwent surgery on his injured knee that cost him the rest of the season. Even Stribling, who started a few games for the 49ers this season, was ruled out due to a season-ending ankle injury. Demarcus Robinson came in later to help bolster the offense, but he too suffered an injury that will keep him out for the next few weeks. If Evans does end up missing the 49ers’ Week 7 tilt against the Atlanta Falcons, their wide receiver room will consist of Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing, and Jordan Watkins. San Francisco does have running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle still, but Brock Purdy will need to make the most of what he’ll be given in the next few weeks. Related: 49ers WR Mike Evans’ Achilles injury gets huge update after MNF win vs. Commanders Related: Of course the Pat McAfee Commanders-49ers MNF broadcast was unhinged

item.title: Report: Mets to Meet with Ex-Hitting Coach About Possible Reunion
item.description: Aug 15, 2016; Phoenix, AZ, USA; New York Mets hitting coach Kevin Long against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Lewis Masella, Site Editor In a search for a new hitting coach, the New York Mets are set to meet and interview Kevin Long on Tuesday for a role on the coaching staff, according to Mike Puma of the New York Post. There is a real possibility the club does in fact reunite with Long, as the two have history with each other. May 3, 2023; Los Angeles, California, USA; Philadelphia Phillies center fielder Brandon Marsh (16) speaks with hitting coach Kevin Long (53) before hitting against the Los Angeles Dodgers during the eighth inning at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-USA TODAY Sports Report: Kevin Long, Mets Set to Meet in Possible Reunion The Mets hired Long ahead of the 2015 season as their hitting coach, and he helped guide them to a National League pennant. The 59-year-old served in that role from 2015 to 2017 and subsequently left after he got passed over for the managerial opening prior to the 2018 season. Kevin Long is scheduled to speak with the Mets tomorrow about a coaching staff position, per source. Long was fired as Phillies hitting coach last week. He was Mets hitting coach the last time the team reached the World Series. He is close with Juan Soto from Nats days. — Mike Puma (@NYPost_Mets) October 19, 2026 On Oct. 6, the Mets announced three coaches would not return to the coaching staff in 2027 — including director of major league hitting Jeff Albert, quality assurance coach Danny Barnes and batting practice pitcher Kevin Mahoney — leaving three vacancies for New York to fill. While all three coaches were told they would not return to the same roles, the Mets are leaving the possibility for them to return in different roles, according to SNY. Long’s 20-year hitting coach career began with the New York Yankees in 2007, and he spent seven seasons in the Bronx, winning the World Series in 2009. After his contract expired with the Mets, Long was hired by the Washington Nationals and won his second World Series with them in 2019. After spending four years in Washington, Long went to Philadelphia. After another set of four years with a team in the NL East, the Phillies fired Long despite having him under contract through 2028 . Long worked with a young Juan Soto , and the two managed to build a relationship that has lasted beyond both of their times in D.C. Long returning to the Mets would give Soto a sense of comfort to know a hitting coach he has good ties with is back. A Connection With a Mets Superstar During his time with the Nationals. Long worked with a young Juan Soto , and the two managed to build a relationship that has lasted beyond both of their times in D.C. Long returning to the Mets would give Soto a sense of comfort to know a hitting coach he has good ties with is back. While Albert departed, Troy Snitker, the current hitting coach, is expected to stay. The question is what responsibilities Long would take on and how the club would divide their hitting instruction, if indeed Long is interviewed for the hitting coach position. The change to the coaching staff this year compared to last year’s is considered minor. That offseason, the Mets had an entire staff overhaul. Jeremy, Hefner, Jeremy Barnes, Eric Chavez, Antoan Richardson, Mike Sarbough, John Gibbons and Glenn Sherlock were among the names that did not return for 2026. Carlos Mendoza , who was recently hired by the Phillies as their infield and third base coach, was let go as manager by President of Baseball Operations David Stearns in late June and replaced by Andy Green . The Last Word A reunion with Long would give the Mets an experienced and respected voice as they look to improve offensively in 2027. That is one area the Mets certainly need to work on as they look to break a two-year postseason drought. For now, the meeting offers both sides a chance to see whether a second stint in Queens is a good fit. item.title: Bears Deliver Bad News on $53 Million Star Ahead of Patriots Game
item.description: Offensive guard Jonah Jackson of the Chicago Bears. Getty Chicago Bears right guard Jonah Jackson. Getty Chicago Bears offensive lineman Luke Newman. Getty The Chicago Bears shared more unfortunate news for their run game via an estimated injury report on Monday, October 19, this time involving elite offensive lineman Jonah Jackson. item.title: ‘Troy Aikman Does Not Want to Be There,’ ‘Looks Normal’ — NFL Fans Split on Cowboys Legend’s ‘Body Language’ on ESPN MNF Amid ‘Tension’ With Joe Buck
item.description: Nov 22, 2012; Arlington, TX, USA; Fox announcers Troy Aikman (left) and Joe Buck on the field prior to the game with the Dallas Cowboys playing against the Washington Redskins on Thanksgiving at Cowboys Stadium. © Matthew Emmons-USA TODAY Sports The contract dispute between Troy Aikman and ESPN is playing out in real time, and more people are starting to take notice of it. After bringing his pairing alongside Joe Buck to be the lead broadcasters for Monday Night Football, the network hasn’t given the Dallas Cowboys legend an extension so far. This week, as the San Francisco 49ers took on the Washington Commanders in the primetime spot, fans were split on the effort and enthusiasm they were seeing from Aikman. Fans Unsure if Troy Aikman Wants to be in MNF Broadcasts After retiring, Aikman joined Fox as an NFL analyst in 2001 and began working with Buck on the network’s top crew the following season. Working at the company for nearly two decades, the two made the switch to ESPN in 2022. That initial contract runs till the end of the 2026 season. So far, the network has signed Buck to a contract extension. But the same luxury hasn’t come through for Aikman. As a result, reports emerged about the two longtime announcers having some tension between them last week. As they opened the broadcast to welcome viewers, fans were already jumping to make sense of what they were seeing. While some believed Aikman wasn’t performing with the same gusto as before, others found his effort commendable. “Troy Aikman does not want to be there,” one fan argued. “I love how Aikman calls everything straight and doesn’t sugarcoat anything. I’m going to guess CBS gets him to pair him with [Jim] Nantz.” After Tony Romo’s legal trouble, CBS and the former Cowboys quarterback mutually agreed to part ways despite four years remaining on his contract. In his place, they’ve given the role alongside Nantz to J.J. Watt. But it’s still unclear if that change is going to be permanent. item.title: All-Star Infielder Released by Yankees Still a Free Agent 171 Days Later
item.description: A former MLB All-Star remains unsigned 171 days after the Yankees released him, raising questions about whether his MLB career will continue. Getty Paul DeJong, a nine-year MLB veteran infielder and 2019 All-Star selection, started the 2026 season as a member of the New York Yankees. But they released him on May 1, and after signing with the Detroit Tigers, he was released by that team as well, on May 25. Now, 147 days after the Tigers released him and 171 days after the Yankees cut ties, DeJong remains a free agent. The 33-year-old infielder did not play a single major league game in 2026, and a season-ending hamstring injury leaves open when, where and whether he returns. DeJong played his last MLB game on Sept. 26, 2025, for the Washington Nationals. That was 388 days ago, as of today, Oct. 19, 2026. The Yankees released DeJong after he exercised an opt-out clause in his minor league contract, according to MLB Trade Rumors. New York had signed him in January as infield depth while Anthony Volpe recovered from shoulder surgery. DeJong hit .203/.361/.516 with six home runs and 16 walks against 18 strikeouts in 23 games for Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, according to CBS Sports . Jose Caballero, Oswaldo Cabrera and Max Schuemann all held 40-man roster spots, leaving DeJong no real path to a big league promotion. Detroit signed him four days later, on May 5, according to the New York Post ’s Jon Heyman . The minor league deal included a prorated $1 million base salary in the majors, according to USA Today ’s Bob Nightengale . But DeJong never got to Detroit. He played six games for the Triple-A Toledo Mud Hens, then limped around the bases while scoring a run on May 12, his last appearance of the season, according to MLB Trade Rumors . The Mud Hens shut him down for the year, and Heyman reported a hamstring injury that required surgery. Toledo released him May 25, according to MLB.com . He joined the Redbirds as a walk-on. The Pittsburgh Pirates drafted him as a catcher in the 38th round in 2014, but DeJong passed on signing and returned to Illinois State for his redshirt junior season, according to MLB.com . The St. Louis Cardinals then took him in the fourth round, 131st overall, in 2015. He debuted May 28, 2017, and homered in his first plate appearance (the ninth Cardinals player to do it). item.title: Rushden fans celebrate league opposition in FA Cup
item.description: Rob Usher and Elliot Sandy joined fans, staff and players to find out who Diamonds had drawn [James Burridge/BBC] Fans and players of eighth-tier AFC Rushden & Diamonds have been celebrating after being drawn an away tie at League One's Burton Albion in the FA Cup. It is the first time the Northern Premier League Division One Midlands side, founded in 2011 following the demise of Rushden & Diamonds, have reached the tournament's first round. Surrounded by about 200 people gathered at the Northamptonshire club for the draw, chairman Rob Usher said: "Let's go put Diamonds back on the map." Kick-off will be at 15:00 BST on 7 November at Albion's home, the Pirelli Stadium in Burton-on-Trent, Staffordshire. Manager Elliot Sandy was just as delighted at the draw, saying: "This was the dream and 15 months later, we've managed to bring that to the club. "This club really deserves it and we're going to enjoy it." He paid tribute to the volunteers, everyone working behind the scenes and his assistant manager. "We've got a great group of lads together, we started brilliant in the league and with everyone behind the scenes, we do the easy bit on the pitch," he added. The FA Cup first round will take place next month [Getty Images] Diamonds secured their place in the first round thanks to a 2-1 upset over National League North outfit Morecambe, who play two leagues above them. They started their FA Cup campaign with a 5-0 win at Kimberley Miners Welfare in August, and have also beaten Long Eaton United, Desborough Town and Peterborough Sports to reach this stage. The club secured their spot in the fourth qualifying round by shocking sixth-tier Braintree Town, of National League South, earlier this month. So, does Usher think Diamonds can beat the League One side? There was, of course, only one answer: "Yes, 100%," he said. However, is it not the only time the Diamonds have played major opposition in the FA Cup. Around the turn of the millennium, the original Rushden & Diamonds reached the FA Cup third round twice - losing to Leeds United and then Sheffield United a season later, after forcing both clubs to a replay. The team reached the heights of Division Two - the equivalent of League One today - soon after, before financial problems led to the club's eventual demise. Do you have a story suggestion for Northamptonshire? Contact us below. Follow Northamptonshire news on BBC Sounds , Facebook , Instagram and X . item.title: UCF Injury Update: Scott Frost Shares Latest on QB Alonza Barnett
item.description: UCF head coach Scott Frost shared the latest injury update on Knights quarterback Alonza Barnett. Getty The UCF Knights are going to be back home on Saturday, this time hosting the BYU Cougars. It’s an extraordinarily tough assignment, as UCF prepares for its highest-ranked opponent ever to visit the Bounce House. Still, coming off two straight Big 12 losses, head coach Scott Frost knows he needs to figure something out quickly. One place UCF could potentially get a boost is if starting quarterback Alonza Barnett was able to return on Saturday. He’s been out since suffering a hamstring injury on September 12th. However, his status remains up in the air. UCF Knights HC Scott Frost on Alonza Barnett On Monday, Scott Frost met with the media. However, he wasn’t ready to share injury updates for this upcoming week. “Not sure on the injuries yet, Alonza or anybody else,” Scott Frost said. “I think we’ll know more tonight and tomorrow. But I think we’re really close to getting a lot of guys back. There is a chance that Frost is playing some games with BYU, hoping not to tip his hand about the UCF injuries. However, one thing is clear, and that’s that Barnett is getting closer to making his return. “Yeah, I think he’s making really good progress,” Frost said. “He looks good. He’s doing a lot of things. I want to make sure he’s ready to go if we put him out there. You know, that position, you might not have to run for 10 plays, and then you’ve got to run away from some really big guys trying to get you. The rest of the game, I know he can do.” Barnett found his success prior to UCF as a dual-threat quarterback. That’s hard to be when you’re battling a hamstring injury. It’s also a concern that Frost noted, because running on an injury can make things worse. “I just want to make sure if he’s out there, he’s not going to get hurt again and he can protect himself. We’re really lucky to have the guys we have in the room. Lights has been doing a really good job,” Frost said. “So we’ll make some decisions when he’s definitely ready to go. But he’s trying really hard. I feel bad for him. This is his last year of college football. He wants to be out there bad. I think he’s willing to be out there even if he’s not 100%. I just want to make sure that he’s capable of protecting himself.” In two games this season, Barnett is completing 63.3% of his passes for 344 yards and 2 touchdowns. He also rushed for a touchdown. The Difference in UCF Quarterbacks One thing Frost clearly wanted last season was to bring experienced quarterbacks to UCF. That started with Barnett, but extended to Keyone Jenkins, who has three years of extensive experience at FIU. He came to presumably back up Barnett, but has been forced into action with the injury. Things have been inconsistent for Jenkins. In particular, poorly timed turnovers and downfield passing have hurt him. item.title: ‘Substation strikes again’ – 49ers fans are upset after Mike Evans’ left game with Achilles injury
item.description: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images San Francisco 49ers WR Mike Evans left the team’s 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders with an apparent Achilles injury. Evans had a strong outing against the Commanders, putting up 94 yards on three receptions through the first two quarters. However, he was absent in the second half after seemingly getting hurt without contact with a minute left in the first half. Evans has dealt with multiple injuries over the last few seasons, and this latest injury, coupled with the 49ers’ shaky injury past, has led to a lot of concern. Mike Evans’ Achilles injury had fans upset After Evans got hurt, fans were quick to react by blaming the electric substation near the 49ers’ training facility, perpetuating a belief that the substation makes players more injury-prone. “Get ’em outta here. No one escapes the Substation,” joked one fan . “Substation strikes again,” said another fan, perpetuating the Substation joke . “Typical Mike, it’s an every-year thing for him. What did y’all expect?” lamented a fan . “Substation putting up Wilt numbers,” joked another fan . “Clearly wasn’t 100% out there. Did he seriously just make his Achilles injury worse in a random game against the Commanders where they would have won regardless? The 49ers don’t do themselves any favours with some of these injuries,” said a fan, blaming the 49ers for their poor approach . Evans came into the game with Achilles issues and missed the week’s scheduled practices. While the team has confirmed that Evans did not tear his Achilles and is expected to miss a little bit of time as compared to suffering a debilitating tear, this is a big concern. The 49ers WR room is depleted with injuries to Deebo Samuel, Ricky Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Christian Kirk. Evans’ absence makes this a much harder situation to bounce back from for the 6-0 49ers. Evans has had 27 receptions on roughly 39 targets for 420 yards this season, converting three touchdowns. item.title: Donovan McNabb’s Tanner McKee Eagles backup QB comments hit very close to home
item.description: Lou Capozzola-USA TODAY NETWORK Donovan McNabb’s Tanner McKee Eagles backup QB comments hit very close to home appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the NFL world continues to grapple with the news that Jalen Hurts’ season is all but over after discovering blood clots in his lungs , the Philadelphia Eagles still have to play games, with Tanner McKee taking over full-time as the team’s interim QB1 . Discussing what he saw from McKee against the Carolina Panthers on 94WIP, Donovan McNabb took a victory lap of sorts on the fans who have been calling for the fourth-year backup to replace Hurts for years, as the results didn’t quite live up to expectations . “Everybody was barking for Tanner McKee over the last couple of years,” McNabb said. “They were saying, ‘Oh, he’s a better passer. He gets the ball out, anticipates his throws. He throws a friendly ball to the receivers.’ Everybody was trying to find everything positive about Tanner McKee. Now, after watching him play, everybody’s like, ‘Oh, well, we miss Jalen.’ Like it never fails. It really does, it never fails. Everybody loves the backup until you see the backup.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Donovan McNabb on comparing Jalen Hurts and Tanner McKee: "Everybody loves the backup until you see the backup." 😳 pic.twitter.com/2YF7HFmSII — SPORTSRADIO 94WIP (@SportsRadioWIP) October 19, 2026 Asked to “come on,” McNabb instead doubled down, reminding listeners that he had to deal with the very same thing throughout his career with reserves like Kevin Kolb and Jeff Garcia back in the day. “I mean, I’ve seen it. I’ve seen it. Yeah, I’ve been a part of it,” McNabb noted. “Everybody loves the backup. You know, when they see a couple, you know, sprinkles in the preseason or he gets in the game because you’re hurt. They say, ‘Well, he should be playing.’ And all of a sudden it’s like, ‘Well, if our starter was in the game,’ It’s like, ‘Okay, now you love me’ when I’m on the sideline. But while I’m in, it’s not enough.” Now granted, maybe McNabb is, in fact, having flashbacks to his own playing career, when fans were calling for a backup to take over at quarterback and finally bring a Super Bowl trophy to the City of Brotherly Love. Maybe he doesn’t like how Hurts was treated in the past and how some are now turning around on QB1 in this new light. But excluding the Hurts of it all, one thing is true: McKee is a very different quarterback for the Eagles, and they will have to get creative to maximize his skill set if they want to win any more games this year. Related: Michael Robinson apologizes for ‘unfounded’ comments on Eagles QB Jalen Hurts’ situation Related: Former Alabama coach Nick Saban shares what he told Jalen Hurts after QB’s concerning update

item.title: Ex-Saints WR Signs With Steelers
item.description: The 49ers placed veteran wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling on injured reserve before Week 7 Getty In a well-traveled NFL career that included a stop with the New Orleans Saints, Marquez Valdes-Scantling has a new contract. On Monday night, The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo reported that the Pittsburgh Steelers are signing MVS to a deal that will start him on the practice squad with the potential to get called up eventually. DeFabo reported the news like this: “A rash of injuries at the wide receiver position has sparked a reunion for the Pittsburgh Steelers. Veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling plans to sign with the Pittsburgh Steelers, a league source told The Athletic. The 31-year-old wide receiver was released by the Los Angeles Chargers over the weekend. He is expected to begin his latest stint with the Steelers on the practice squad.” It’s a reunion with Aaron Rodgers, who initially played with Valdes-Scantling with the Green Bay Packers ,” DeFabo writes. “The Green Bay Packers drafted Valdes-Scantling in 2018, which was Mike McCarthy’s final season in Green Bay. For four years with Aaron Rodgers, Valdes-Scantling caught 123 passes for 2,153 yards and 13 touchdowns. When the Steelers were struggling to find reliable targets behind DK Metcalf a year ago, Rodgers publicly lobbied for Valdes-Scantling. The QB called the receiver one of his ‘favorite’ teammates of all time. In five games with the Steelers last season, Valdes-Scantling caught 10 passes and a touchdown.” Marquez Valdes-Scantling With Saints Valdes-Scantling was a member of the Saints in the second half of the 2024 sesaon. He had begun that campaign with the Buffalo Bills , but they released him on Oct. 15, 2024, and the Saints signed him on Oct. 21. MVS got eight games with the Saints and was targeted 35 times. He caught 17 of those for 385 yards and four touchdowns. It was a bit of a throwback for Valdes-Scantling, who averaged 22.6 yards per catch with the Saints. He once led the NFL in yards per reception while playing for the Packers in 2020, so the fact that Valdes-Scantling rediscovered his younger self in New Orleans may have helped prolong his NFL career. He left the Saints after that season and split 2025 between the 49ers and Steelers, then began the 2026 season with the Chargers. Now he’s back in Pittsburgh. MVS in Steelers Depth Chart The Steelers are pretty buried on their WR depth chart at the moment. DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard are the only two healthy guys they really trust. Ben Skowronek is hurting, and Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. are already on injured reserve. Valdes-Scantling has a chance to help, for sure. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Ex-Saints WR Signs With Steelers appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Commanders’ $45 Million Defender Suffers Knee Injury vs. 49ers
item.description: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 20: Javon Kinlaw #99 of the Washington Commanders reacts to a sack during a game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty Right when things seemed like they couldn’t get worse for the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers … well, they did. After NFL All-Pro wide receiver Terry McLaurin left the game and was ruled out with a serious knee injury in the first half, $45 million defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw suffered the same fate and was ruled out with a knee injury early in the third quarter. “Javon Kinlaw (knee) ruled out,” ESPN’s John Keim wrote on his official X account on Monday night. “Javon Kinlaw has been ruled out with a knee injury,” The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala wrote on his official X account. “This is quietly a huge loss for the Commanders,” Commanders reporter Chad Ryan wrote on X . “ Kinlaw is important and effective up front.” DT Javon Kinlaw (knee) is out pic.twitter.com/WCWTOCevrQ — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 20, 2026 This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Commanders’ $45 Million Defender Suffers Knee Injury vs. 49ers appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Former Chiefs Starting QB Could Help Eagles Replace Jalen Hurts
item.description: The Chiefs fear the worst for QB Gardner Minshew's injury. Getty A Kansas City Chiefs quarterback who filled in for Patrick Mahomes could once again find himself replacing an injured star. Journeyman Gardner Minshew has been named as a top trade candidate in the weeks before the NFL deadline, with the struggling Arizona Cardinals looking to sell off assets. That could create an opportunity for the Philadelphia Eagles, who will need some help after Jalen Hurts was ruled out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. New Opportunity for Gardner Minshew Minshew was pushed into action last season after Mahomes suffered a season-ending knee injury, though his tenure was short-lived. Minshew completed 6-of-13 passes for 37 yards with one interception and no touchdowns before he suffered a season-ending injury of his own. Minshew could have another chance this year, with CBS Sports reporter Carter Bahns predicting the Cardinals could use him as trade bait. “With one in-season trade already complete, the Cardinals have established themselves as sellers,” Bahns wrote. “Other teams will likely call to see just how many players they are willing to part with, as the team seems destined for a last-place finish in the NFC West and is liquidating pieces that do not fit into first-year coach Mike LaFleur’s system.” Bahns suggested the Cardinals might want a look at a promising young quarterback, which would make Minshew redundant. “And with the potential for the Cardinals to activate Carson Beck as their backup quarterback, the likelihood of them keeping Minshew around as a No. 3 option decreases,” Bahns wrote. Eagles Could Call on Former Chiefs QB for Help The Eagles will likely need more depth after losing Hurts to what is expected to be a season-ending setback. The Eagles quarterback was initially diagnosed with a blood clot after taking a cleat to his calf area in an October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams , but an examination later found clots in his lungs as well. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said he trusts the team’s medical staff to care for Hurts, who is expected to make a full recovery. “I’m not a medical expert,” Sirianni said, via The Associated Press . “I lean on our guys in all those situations. I’m a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them. It’s not just me that has major care for our players. It’s them, as well.” Though the Eagles turned to Tanner McKee in Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers , they will likely need more help. Minshew has plenty of NFL experience, including a two-year stint with the Eagles in 2021 and 2022 where he appeared in nine games with four starts. He has 47 starts across a seven-year career, completing 63.1% of his passes for 11,987 yards with 68 touchdowns and 35 interceptions. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Former Chiefs Starting QB Could Help Eagles Replace Jalen Hurts appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Rays superstar Junior Caminero pays Randy Arozarena with perfect homage after Game 6 blast
item.description: Jordan Johnson-Imagn Images Rays superstar Junior Caminero pays Randy Arozarena with perfect homage after Game 6 blast appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero delivered more than a crucial home run on Monday night, paying tribute to former teammate Randy Arozarena during Game 6 of the American League Championship Series. The 23-year-old blasted a two-run homer off Cleveland Guardians reliever Cade Smith in the seventh inning at Tropicana Field. The shot struck the left-field foul pole, extending Tampa Bay’s lead to 5-1. However, Caminero’s celebration provided another memorable moment as the Rays closed in on their first World Series appearance since 2020. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) During his home-run trot, Caminero looked toward Arozarena in the stands before crossing his arms to recreate the former Rays outfielder’s signature celebration. MLB shared footage of the tribute Monday on X, formerly Twitter, capturing Caminero acknowledging Arozarena before crossing home plate. Junior Caminero looked toward Randy Arozarena and did Randy's celebration before crossing home! pic.twitter.com/ehAH0ZrpYx — MLB (@MLB) October 20, 2026 The moment connected two generations of Rays postseason stars during Tampa Bay’s eventual 7-3 victory over the Guardians. Arozarena, now with the Seattle Mariners, helped lead the Rays to the 2020 World Series. His postseason performance that year established him as one of the franchise’s most recognizable playoff figures. Meanwhile, Caminero entered the postseason following a 42-home-run regular season. His seventh-inning blast marked his first career playoff homer and provided valuable insurance in the decisive contest. Arozarena attended Monday’s game alongside former Rays pitcher Tyler Glasnow, another member of Tampa Bay’s 2020 pennant-winning team. The Rays ultimately completed a 4-2 ALCS victory, advancing to their third World Series in franchise history. Tampa Bay now turns its attention to the Milwaukee Brewers, with Game 1 scheduled for Friday at American Family Field. Both franchises are pursuing their first World Series championship, setting up a historic matchup that will guarantee a first-time champion. Related: Kevin Cash’s post-ALCS comments will have Rays fans booking flights to Milwaukee Related: Rays pitcher Freddy Peralta couldn’t imagine World Series run before Mets trade to Tampa

item.title: Luke, 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey share awesome jersey exchange after MNF
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Luke, 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey share awesome jersey exchange after MNF appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Monday Night Football was the McCaffrey Bowl as brothers Christian and Luke McCaffrey went up against one another. Christian wound up being the star of the game as he had 117 total yards and two touchdowns to help the 49ers get the 23-17 win over Luke’s Washington Commander’s. After the game, the brothers posed for a cool jersey exchange and hug. The McCaffrey brothers exchange jerseys after a hard-fought game ❤️ pic.twitter.com/aFfOUSwUc2 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — 49ers on NBCS (@NBCS49ers) October 20, 2026 Early on, the game looked like it was going to be a blowout as the 49ers built up a 20-3 halftime lead thanks to two first-half Christian McCaffrey touchdowns. But the Commanders fought back in the second half and very nearly tied the game late. However, it could have been very different had Luke McCaffrey touched the ball in a potential special teams fiasco during the start of the fourth quarter. If he did, the 49ers would have had the ball near the red zone. But replays showed he did not touch the ball, so the Commanders were able to keep possession. Despite missing star receiver Terry McLaurin to a knee injury early, the Commanders were able to mount a second-half comeback. Jayden Daniels relied on Chig Okonkwo and Treylon Burks in McLaurin’s absence, and they delivered with 11 catches for 135 yards. Stefon Diggs also did his part with a touchdown, his fourth of the season. The Commanders fell just short in the end, though, as they dropped to 1-4-1 on the season. Meanwhile, the 49ers maintained their 100% record on the season. They will put that perfect 6-0 mark on the line next week away to the Atlanta Falcons. Related: 49ers WR Mike Evans’ Achilles injury gets huge update after MNF win vs. Commanders Related: Of course the Pat McAfee Commanders-49ers MNF broadcast was unhinged

Stefon Diggs also did his part with a touchdown, his fourth of the season. The Commanders fell just short in the end, though, as they dropped to 1-4-1 on the season. Meanwhile, the 49ers maintained their 100% record on the season. They will put that perfect 6-0 mark on the line next week away to the Atlanta Falcons. Related: 49ers WR Mike Evans’ Achilles injury gets huge update after MNF win vs. Commanders Related: Of course the Pat McAfee Commanders-49ers MNF broadcast was unhinged

item.title: ‘It’s Pathetic,’ ‘How Much Did the PR Team Pay You?’ — Fans Slam NFL Insider’s ‘Damage Control’ for Eagles After Jalen Hurts’ Diagnosis
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts. After losing star quarterback Jalen Hurts to a medical condition expected to sideline him for the rest of the 2026 season, the Philadelphia Eagles have found themselves dealing with another controversy. It’s about how the team handled his injury and the backlash that followed. The controversy began when Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported that Hurts had been awake for “roughly 36 hours” after doctors diagnosed him with a superficial blood clot before his Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. The report sparked backlash, with many accusing the Eagles of downplaying the severity of Hurts’ condition, which is expected to end his season. Tom Pelissero Faces Backlash After Clarifying Jalen Hurts’ Sleep Timeline Pelissero’s initial report framed Hurts’ decision to play as a show of commitment. However, after critics questioned whether the situation should be celebrated, the insider clarified that Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, later told him that the quarterback slept after returning to the team from the hospital. The Eagles had apparently arranged a room for Hurts at the stadium before kickoff. The clarification only fueled further criticism, with some fans accusing Pelissero of misleading them. One fan reacted to the updated account, writing , “So you clickbaited us.” Another questioned the change in Pelissero’s report, saying , “In other words, your original post made the Eagles look bad, and they made you retract your statement. It’s pathetic what y’all are doing.” Fans also questioned why the original report wasn’t verified before publication. One X user challenged Pelissero’s reporting process, writing , “So you’re a ‘reporter’ who made this serious, serious claim (wrapped in a tone-deaf message about commitment) without even talking to the player’s agent first and got major info wrong? item.title: Manchester City vs AEK Athens: Here is the latest City injury news and predicted City starting eleven
item.description: Manchester City vs AEK Athens: Here is the latest City injury news and predicted City starting eleven Manchester City will play their third match of the UEFA Champions League league phase tonight when they take on AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium. Enzo Maresca’s side have won one game and lost one in their opening two Champions League matches. They beat FC Porto on match day one but were beaten by PSG on match day two. AEK Athens have also won one match and lost one after beating LASK in their opening match before being beaten 3-1 by Shakhtar Donetsk last week. Both teams will be desperate to pick up three points to gain a footing in their UEFA Champions League league phase. Here is the latest City injury news and my predicted Manchester City starting eleven for tonight’s match. Latest City injury and team news. Antoine Semenyo will miss tonight’s match due to a knee injury. The powerful winger will be out of action for the next eight weeks, as revealed by Enzo Maresca yesterday . Losing Semenyo for a sustained period of time is a huge blow for Manchester City. But his misfortune does give an opportunity for others to play a more prominent role in Manchester City’s attack. Erling Haaland, Matheus Nunes, Mateo Kovacic and Nico O’Reilly all failed to take part in Manchester City’s open training session yesterday. It would seem that all four players’ participation in tonight’s match is in doubt. Selecting tonight’s starting eleven doesn’t seem like a straightforward task for Enzo Maresca. There is strength in depth in the City squad. Tonight may be the night where he rotates his squad. That does seem like a realistic option given that Manchester City play Aston Villa at Villa Park on Saturday. It does seem like tonight may be the night for Rico Lewis, Vitor Reis and Allan to start but it remains to be seen if that is a route that Enzo Maresca explores. Predicted City starting eleven.

item.title: Angel Reese’s post after Dream’s historic Game 2 win immediately goes viral
item.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Angel Reese’s post after Dream’s historic Game 2 win immediately goes viral appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Angel Reese was the driving force in the Atlanta Dream ’s victory over the Golden State Valkyries, 79-65, in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center on Monday. The Dream tied the best-of-seven series at 1-1. Reese finished with a double-double of 30 points and 16 rebounds, becoming the youngest player in league history to post such numbers in the WNBA Finals . The 26-year-old forward added three assists and two blocks in 34 minutes. Atlanta’s win was a watershed moment, as it was the team’s first ever in the WNBA Finals. The Dream went to the ultimate round in 2010, 2011, and 2013, but they got swept in all of them. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After the game, Reese posted a five-word message on X. “DUBS IN THE MF CHAT,” wrote the Defensive Player of the Year. It swiftly went viral, as fans heaped praise on Reese. “LSU ANGEL CAME OUT TONIGHT. GO GET THAT RING, CINCO,” said @___lovelanii. “In Angel we trust. Big W tonight!” echoed @Clai_Thompson. “THAT’S HOW YOU HOOP 🔥,” wrote @AlexMvck. “WELCOME TO ANGELHALLA! They should name it after you! Way to ball! Way to win! Let’s go home! ♥️♥️🅰️🅰️🅰️,” commented @KeepitondLO13. “You did your BIG one! 👏🏾👏🏾👏🏾👏🏾,” added @D_Aiche_Jay. “I’m just an old girlie who may have missed her window, but you are truly an inspiration to everyone! Keep. Going. Angel. Reese,” stated @PettyLupone. Reese walked the talk after claiming that the Valkyries did not do anything to “mess up” the Dream in Game 1. Reese, who shared a special moment with Sheryl Swoopes after Game 2, set the tempo, scoring 15 points on 6-of-9 shooting in the first half. She did not take her foot off the gas. She said she is eager to see Atlanta “pull up” and “pop out” in Game 3 on Wednesday. Related: Why did Dream win Game 2 vs. Valkyries? Allisha Gray’s 2-word answer is epic Related: Dream’s Angel Reese reveals Liberty stars’ message that is fueling her in WNBA Finals

item.title: LeBron James Criticized For Old Dalton Knecht Lakers Quote
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 19: LeBron James #23 of the Los Angeles Lakers celebrates his dunk with teammate Dalton Knecht #4 while playing the Utah Jazz during the fourth quarter of the Emirates NBA Cup at Crypto.com Arena on November 19, 2024 in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty The Los Angeles Lakers made big news by getting rid of Dalton Knecht today to follow the NBA roster size rules. Many Lakers fans are disappointed since it wasn’t that long ago that Knecht was expected to be a major part of the future. The Lakers drafted Knecht with the 17 th overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft as a sharpshooter from three-point range. Unfortunately, things didn’t pan out and Knecht is now out of a job. LeBron James is getting dragged into this story, despite no longer being on the Lakers. An old quote from LeBron resurfaced with fans calling out for it: “They didn’t find didn’t find DK… the other 16 teams f****d it up. Did anybody watch him?” James publicly criticized the 16 teams who selected other rookies over Knecht and implied he’d be a big piece for the Lakers. A popular belief exists that the Lakers drafted Knecht for LeBron to give him another shooter to pass to. Knecht showed some flashes of potential before the Lakers placed him in a trade to the Charlotte Hornet s. Injury concerns with Mark Williams saw the Lakers backing out and bringing back Knecht where things fell apart. Why LeBron James Publicly Vouched For Dalton Knecht The comment from LeBron was bold since he didn’t have to say anything too bold beyond offering support. However, it turns out that James truly believed in Knecht and hoped he would become part of the Lakers’ young core with rising star Austin Reaves . LeBron also went on the record for Reaves before anyone knew too much about him to show his vision. The problem is that James also has a negative track record for influencing draft picks. Shabazz Napier was a prospect that LeBron once vouched for having All-Star potential. The Miami Heat drafted Napier to impress James, but he left them anyway in free agency for the Cleveland Cavaliers . Napier never materialized into a star and showed LeBron’s eye for talent can fail badly. Knecht may be of the same tier as a player that James saw something special in during his college tenure that couldn’t translate to the NBA. LeBron James Was Rooting Against Dalton Knecht The current context of the Lakers decision likely saw LeBron rooting for his son Bronny James to keep his roster spot. Lakers management had to release one player and saw Bronny on that short list of realistic names who could be cut. Lakers management had to release one player and saw Bronny on that short list of realistic names who could be cut. The shooting of Knecht never thriving saw head coach JJ Redick fully losing confidence in him last season. Los Angeles backing out of the Hornets trade saw Knecht never mentally recovering from that to make the most of his playing time. Another team will likely take the chance on Knecht due to his age, but his clock is ticking. Knecht must make the most of his next opportunity or find his way out of the NBA for good. item.title: Rays’ Freddy Peralta wins ALCS MVP before facing former team Brewers in World Series
item.description: Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Rays’ Freddy Peralta wins ALCS MVP before facing former team Brewers in World Series appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . What a difference a few months have made for Freddy Peralta . Prior to the trade deadline, he was a struggling pitcher who performed to the tune of a 4.99 ERA with the New York Mets following a blockbuster offseason trade from the Milwaukee Brewers. After the Tampa Bay Rays acquired him, he seems to have found a new lease in life — culminating in this incredible postseason achievement. Peralta, who started Game 6 of the ALCS between the Rays and the Cleveland Guardians, ended up having another brilliant outing. He allowed just one earned run in 5.1 innings of work. This comes just two days after he appeared in relief, getting two outs for Tampa Bay in a crucial Game 4 victory. As a result, the Rays’ trade deadline acquisition earned ALCS MVP honors for being a reliable force on their way to a World Series berth. The 30-year-old starting pitcher also took the mound for Game 2 of the ALCS , recording six innings of shutout baseball. In three appearances in the ALCS, Peralta recorded an ERA of 0.75 in 12.0 innings — with the Rays winning in all three games he pitched in. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This is a continuation of the improvements Peralta has shown ever since the Rays brought him in at the deadline. He has not allowed more than one earned run in any appearance since the 27th of August, spanning a total of 10 appearances (nine starts). In 14 total appearances for the Rays thus far (regular season and postseason combined), Peralta has put up a sterling ERA of 2.75 in 72.0 innings — a stunning return to form. But the emotional rollercoaster for Peralta is only about to get wilder. The Rays will be facing his former team, the Brewers, in the World Series; Peralta spent the first eight seasons of his MLB career in Milwaukee, so he is at least going to be a bit familiar with those standing in the way of his quest to win his and the Rays’ first World Series title. Related: Kevin Cash’s post-ALCS comments will have Rays fans booking flights to Milwaukee Related: Rays pitcher Freddy Peralta couldn’t imagine World Series run before Mets trade to Tampa

item.title: ‘Commanders’ Season Is Over,’ ‘A Fireable Offense’ — NFL Analysts React to Washington’s MNF Loss to 49ers, Call for Dan Quinn’s Job
item.description: 'Commanders' Season Is Over,' 'A Fireable Offense' -- NFL Analysts React to Washington's MNF Loss to 49ers, Call for Dan Quinn's Job The Washington Commanders’ season is threatening to unravel after another frustrating Monday night, with a 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers leaving them at 1-4-1. The Commanders trailed 20-3 at halftime against San Francisco before mounting a second-half comeback, but another questionable decision from Jayden Daniels and continued concerns about head coach Dan Quinn and his staff have left the team facing serious questions heading into its bye week. NFL Analysts Call for Dan Quinn to Be Fired With Washington struggling to find consistency and Terry McLaurin leaving the game with a knee injury, PFN asked our NFL analysts for their thoughts on the Commanders’ outlook and whether Quinn’s time with the franchise is running out. Caleb Yaccarino had the strongest take on what the loss should mean for the Commanders and believes the coaching staff is preventing Daniels from reaching his potential. “Jayden Daniels has unlimited potential and can lead this team to wins, but coaching is holding him back, and constantly putting him in situations that risk his long-term health is a fireable offense,” Yaccarino wrote. “Add that to the long list of reasons the Commanders should move on from Dan Quinn, which must happen at some point this season.” Daniels is currently ranked 15th in PFN’s QB Impact Score with a grade of 77.8 through six weeks, while the team’s offense as a whole is ranked 20th with a 73.2 grade in PFN’s Offense Impact Score . Jason Katz doesn’t see the season getting any better for Washington after repeated blunders and called for the organization not to delay the eventual firing of its head coach. “The Commanders are still playing hard for Quinn, but the decision has to be about more than that. Too many in-game blunders. Too many penalties. Too much lack of discipline,” Katz said. “That falls on the coach. This team is very clearly going nowhere this year. If you’re gonna fire Quinn after the season, just do it now.” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Jacob Infante was equally blunt, saying, “The Commanders’ season is over, and it’s looking like the writing is on the wall for Dan Quinn’s future with the team. I don’t believe they have the offensive firepower anymore to consistently win games, even in a miserable NFC East.” Brandon Astreicher also called for Quinn’s firing, writing , “I feel bad for the Commanders. It [expletive] when your coach chooses to help your opponent. Dan Quinn has to be fired. “Peewee-level mistakes every week; it’s frankly embarrassing,” he continued, while also adding that with Quinn gone, Washington may have a chance to give it a run in the “awful” NFC East race. Dan Quinn has to be fired. “Peewee-level mistakes every week; it’s frankly embarrassing,” he continued, while also adding that with Quinn gone, Washington may have a chance to give it a run in the “awful” NFC East race. On the other hand, Brandon Austin differed slightly from the last message, noting that the Commanders might not have a chance in the NFC East anymore. “Dan Quinn’s days are numbered. Jayden Daniels has also made some unacceptable blunders. But it starts at the top, and you have to ask: what does Quinn add to this football team?” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Kyle Soppe, meanwhile, acknowledged the Commanders’ fightback in the second half after trailing 20-3 at halftime. Still, he believes the bye week would be a perfect window to make changes, but he doesn’t see a major turnaround for the team, even if a new head coach replaces Quinn. “The Commanders aren’t going anywhere, but they showed nice battle in a game they had no business having a shot to win. A change during the bye tracks, as the rest of this season is a low-stakes operation, but I’m not sure anyone is having success at the head of this ship for the remainder of 2026.” The Commanders and Daniels will return home in Week 8 to face the Philadelphia Eagles. Whether that will be with Quinn or a new head coach remains to be seen. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Red Bull had three F1 stars in their hands – and let all three slip away
item.description: Christian Horner has disclosed that Red Bull had the opportunity to evaluate George Russell , Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri before any of them reached Formula 1 , with all three drivers impressing during sessions on the team's simulator. However, despite their performances attracting attention within the organisation, none eventually became part of Red Bull's junior programme. The former Red Bull team principal shared the story during an appearance on the High Performance Podcast, explaining that the three drivers had used the team's facilities while pursuing their ambitions of reaching Formula 1. Their simulator sessions were privately funded by their families, who paid Red Bull for access to the equipment. Although the drivers were not officially associated with the team's development programme, their performances reportedly stood out when compared with those of the youngsters already supported by Red Bull. Russell, Norris and Piastri would eventually follow different routes into Formula 1, joining rival manufacturers' junior programmes before securing their places on the grid. Russell became a Mercedes junior driver and made his Formula 1 debut with Williams in 2019, while Norris joined McLaren's development programme before earning his first race seat that same year. Piastri, meanwhile, was supported by Renault and Alpine during his junior career before moving to McLaren for his Formula 1 debut in 2023. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Horner reveals how Red Bull were warned about Norris, Russell, and Piastri Reflecting on the early encounters with the drivers, Horner explained that Red Bull's simulator operator had been particularly impressed by their abilities, even suggesting they were outperforming some of the team's existing prospects. "I remember George Russell was paying us to go on our simulator, and as was Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, their dads were writing checks for them to run on the driver simulator that we had. The guy that was looking after it was coming up to me and saying, 'Christian, these kids are better than the juniors we've got at the moment.'" The feedback was significant enough for Horner to raise the matter with Helmut Marko, who oversaw Red Bull's driver development programme and played a central role in identifying young talent for the organisation: "I remember taking them to Helmut and going, 'I really think you should look at these guys.'" Nevertheless, the three drivers continued their careers outside the Red Bull system, eventually establishing themselves at rival Formula 1 teams, with Norris even going on to win the 2025 title after defeating Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the title battle. Looking back at the situation, Horner jokingly expressed his frustration at seeing the drivers achieve success elsewhere, delivering a typically blunt assessment of the missed opportunity: "Wankers. Look who that, turned out well for in the end."

item.description: Tottenham are level with Beyoncé at last. Progress is represented in Roberto De Zerbi’s side earning only their sixth home win in the Premier League since November 2024. Cynics will point out that this spectacular stadium has hosted as many Beyoncé gigs during that time, but Spurs are finally singing a happier tune after dragging themselves out of the bottom three thanks to a messy but gritty 3-1 win over Coventry. It was not especially convincing. Coventry raged at the second Spurs goal, delivered when Omar Marmoush responded to Jack Rudoni’s equaliser for the visitors with a vicious effort in the 59th minute. Relief poured out of Marmoush after his first goal since joining on loan from Manchester City, but should it have stood? The Egyptian forward, who otherwise had a quiet game, was fortunate not to be penalised for an elbow on Milan van Ewijk. Continue reading...

Relief poured out of Marmoush after his first goal since joining on loan from Manchester City, but should it have stood? The Egyptian forward, who otherwise had a quiet game, was fortunate not to be penalised for an elbow on Milan van Ewijk. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father, Richard, made a career as a footballer in England; his brother, Alfie, was coming through Leeds’s academy; Charlie was on the fringes of the Leeds first team when the opportunity to join Toulouse arose in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play,” says Cresswell, now at Rennes and preparing to face Juventus in the Europa League. Continue reading...

item.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
item.description: Centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle. So, another win for Arsenal : their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes. Continue reading...

item.title: Semenyo’s eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for Haaland
item.description: Ghana forward sustained knee injury against Ipswich Maresca to ring changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday. Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing against Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday. Maresca has said he will make changes and has admitted previously that Haaland will require resting at some point. Semenyo would have been the most obvious replacement but Phil Foden and Iliman Ndiaye could be utilised. Continue reading...

item.title: Bayern and Luis Díaz warm up for Arsenal revenge mission with furious rout of Leipzig | Andy Brassell
item.description: Bruised Bundesliga champions hit a supposed rival for six and their flying winger is peaking at a perfect moment When Bayern Munich fail to win for two games in a row, you know what is coming next. Particularly on a Saturday night showcase, against the sort of good domestic opposition that tend to bring the best out of the champions. It had been a frustrating week, domestically and continentally, in two games on the road. On both occasions they had been caught cold, conceding the Bundesliga’s fastest goal at Augsburg and going 1-0 down in less than 90 seconds in Stavanger . Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, almost motionless in his seat as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. The sporting director, Max Eberl, who stood in for his coach in the post-match press conference, explained that the Belgian had been ill, not to mention Kompany’s current hip problem that had made the move from dressing room to pitchside slow and uncomfortable. Continue reading...

Wiegman, who took on the role in September 2021 , also led her native Netherlands side to European Championship glory in 2017 and has reached the final of the past five major tournaments, twice finishing as a World Cup runner-up. item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I suffer a lot’: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig on not enjoying games and the prospect of Liverpool | Sid Lowe
item.description: It will be a tense time for Europe’s longest serving president, despite the Champions League game at Anfield offering a symbol of how far they have come The first time Fernando Roig watched Villarreal play as their president, he sat in the stand at a tiny whitewashed ground that had concrete fever and was half empty. It was a Sunday night in the second division, they lost 3-0 against Badajoz, and he didn’t enjoy it much. But then, he never enjoys it much. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous,” he says. “It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious. I suffer a lot. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich
item.description: There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats”, but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games. Ipswich were the latest victims, but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to have breached financial rules . Defiance has fortified most of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an emblem of their wealth, Erling Haaland, secured the points to move six clear, albeit with a few scares between, courtesy of Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City are suddenly box-office in age of charge-rage and mega defiance | Barney Ronay
item.description: This is by far the most interesting this club have ever been and they faced PSG, a kind of twin entity in all this as oil state glove puppets Another day, another note of unreality; another vivid and brilliant spectacle that feels as though it has been whipped together out of meringue and burnt sugar. Time flies when the world is closing in. Two weeks on, this was Manchester City’s first home game since the verdict dropped, the irrefutable body of evidence was refuted, and English football entered its state of ongoing whiplash. In the stadium this felt like watching someone dance while the world burns. This was a brilliant game pegged out around six goals , a collapse, a comeback, posts and bars struck, saved penalties, and a performance of state-of-the-art omni-football from this brilliantly high-grade Paris Saint-Germain team. Continue reading...
